Saʿd, al-Mujālid b. Saʿīd is Abū ʿUmayr Mujālid b. Saʿīd al-Hamdānī, and died in 144/761 (<a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV06P349A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 6 p. 349)). Ibn Isḥāq is not listed as one of those who related from him, nor is Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. His full name appears to have been Abū Saʿīd Mujālid b. Saʿīd b. Mujālid b. ʿUmayr b. Dhī Murrām b. Shurḥabīl b. Rabīʿah b. Marthad b. Jashm al-Hamdānī. According <a href="../references.html#ref-TKHL" class="source-ref">TKHLV01P686B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ al-Shaybānī al-ʿAṣfarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ</span>, vol. 1 p. 686) he died in 143 or 144. There is a Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥuṣayn al-Tamīmī who related to Ibn Isḥāq. IN <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī), on the story of the blessings on ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf, see <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV03P098B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 3 p. 98), <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV44P183A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 44 p. 183), <a href="../references.html#ref-IAUB" class="source-ref">IAUBV02P907B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Usāmah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Bughyat al-bāḥith ʿan zawāʾid Musnad al-Ḥārith</span>, vol. 2 p. 907), THSAV01P256B, <a href="../references.html#ref-NSSX" class="source-ref">NSSXV03P251A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥākim al-Nīsābūrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Mustadrak ʿalā al-ṣaḥīḥīn</span>, vol. 3 p. 251), <a href="../references.html#ref-NYMX" class="source-ref">NYMXV01P121A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Nuʿaym</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Maʿrifat al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 1 p. 121), <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV35P285A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 35 p. 285), <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV35P285B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 35 p. 285), AMKAV01P104B, and <a href="../references.html#ref-HYGH" class="source-ref">HYGHV03P378F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī b. Abī Bakr Haythamī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ghāyat al-muqṣad fī zawāʾid al-musnad</span>, vol. 3 p. 378); and on the account of Saʿd b. Abī Waqqāṣ’ prayer practices, see <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV03P064A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 3 p. 64), <a href="../references.html#ref-RJXX" class="source-ref">RJXXV03P242B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Maqdisī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Aḥādīth al-mukhtārah</span>, vol. 3 p. 242), and <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHR" class="source-ref">KTHRV03P383B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Jāmiʿ al-masānīd waʾl-sunan</span>, vol. 3 p. 383). He is also listed in traditions found in <a href="WSFAB.html" class="witness-link">WSFAB</a> (Salamah b. al-Faḍl al-Abrash al-Azraqī al-Anṣārī al-Rāzī): on the story of the ʿAmālīq attack on the Ḥijāz see, <a href="../references.html#ref-BBKH" class="source-ref">BBKHV05P108A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Isḥāq b. al-ʿAbbās al-Makkī al-Fākihī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Akhbār makkah fī qadīm al-dahr wa-ḥadīthih</span>, vol. 5 p. 108) and <a href="../references.html#ref-SHBH" class="source-ref">SHBHV01P458B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Aḥmad b. ʿAlī al-Fāsī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Shifāʼ al-gharām bi-akhbār al-Balad al-ḥarām</span>, vol. 1 p. 458); Muḥammad’s invitation to the Kindah, see <a href="../references.html#ref-TBRB" class="source-ref">TBRBV02P349B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk (1967)</span>, vol. 2 p. 349); and in the story of Muḥammad’s and Abū Bakr’s flight from Mecca, see <a href="../references.html#ref-TBRB" class="source-ref">TBRBV02P377B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk (1967)</span>, vol. 2 p. 377). <a href="WZATB.html" class="witness-link">WZATB</a> (Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ṭufayl al-Kūfī al-Bakkāʾī al-ʿĀmirī): on the invitation to the <em>banū</em> ʿAbd Allāh see, <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P424D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 424) and on the aftermath of the killing of ʿUthmān, see <a href="../references.html#ref-TMMX" class="source-ref">TMMXV01P080B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Aḥmad al-Tamīmī al-Maghribī al-Ifrīrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Miḥan</span>, vol. 1 p. 80). <a href="WYBWS.html" class="witness-link">WYBWS</a> (Yūnus b. Bukayr b. Wāṣil al-Shaybānī al-Jamāl al-Kūfī): on the Battle of Dhāt al-Salāsil see <a href="../references.html#ref-BQWX" class="source-ref">BQWXV04P399B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Dalāʾil al-nubūwah wa maʿarifah aḥwāl ṣāḥib al-sharīʿah</span>, vol. 4 p. 399), <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV02P023C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 2 p. 23), <a href="../references.html#ref-THRX" class="source-ref">THRXV04P232A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Athīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Usd al-ghābah fī maʿrifat al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 4 p. 232), <a href="../references.html#ref-DHTI" class="source-ref">DHTIV02P514B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dhahabī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-Islām</span>, vol. 2 p. 514), and <a href="../references.html#ref-DHSL" class="source-ref">DHSLV02P100C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dhahabī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Siyar aʿlām al-nubalāʾ</span>, vol. 2 p. 100); on the death scene of the prophet, see <a href="../references.html#ref-BQWX" class="source-ref">BQWXV07P260C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Dalāʾil al-nubūwah wa maʿarifah aḥwāl ṣāḥib al-sharīʿah</span>, vol. 7 p. 260), <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHS" class="source-ref">KTHSV04P532C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrat al-nubuwīyah</span>, vol. 4 p. 532), and <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHB" class="source-ref">KTHBV05P267D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bidāyat waʾl-nihāyah</span>, vol. 5 p. 267); and on the story of Abū Bakr’s efforts to bring potential converts to Muḥammad (also found in <a href="WZATB.html" class="witness-link">WZATB</a> (Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ṭufayl al-Kūfī al-Bakkāʾī al-ʿĀmirī) on <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P249F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 249)), see <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV30P044B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 30 p. 44) , <a href="../references.html#ref-THRX" class="source-ref">THRXV03P311A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Athīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Usd al-ghābah fī maʿrifat al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 3 p. 311), <a href="../references.html#ref-DHTI" class="source-ref">DHTIV01P126B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dhahabī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-Islām</span>, vol. 1 p. 126) , and <a href="../references.html#ref-DHSL" class="source-ref">DHSLV01P204B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dhahabī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Siyar aʿlām al-nubalāʾ</span>, vol. 1 p. 204)). Finaly, <a href="WJHZA.html" class="witness-link">WJHZA</a> (Jarīr b. Ḥāzim b. Zayd b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Shajāʿ al-Azdī al-ʿAtkī al-Baṣrī); on the story of the death scene of Muḥammad, see <a href="../references.html#ref-BQWX" class="source-ref">BQWXV07P260C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Dalāʾil al-nubūwah wa maʿarifah aḥwāl ṣāḥib al-sharīʿah</span>, vol. 7 p. 260). <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV01P156F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 1 p. 156) states that Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥuṣayn al-Tamīmī was, according to what Ibn Isḥāq told Yūnus b. Bukayr, a “staunch faster” (صواما قواما), indicating that Ibn Isḥāq might have known him well. Al-Bukharī goes on to say that Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Bakkāʾī related traditions from Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān via Ibn Isḥāq, but he does not mention other witnesses. It should be noted that al-Bukharī provides a separate biography for a Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allāh, who, he implies, is not the same person as Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥuṣayn al-Tamīmī, who also related to Ibn Isḥāq through <a href="WYBWS.html" class="witness-link">WYBWS</a> (Yūnus b. Bukayr b. Wāṣil al-Shaybānī al-Jamāl al-Kūfī) (<a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV01P158B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 1 p. 158)), but he does not say he is different directly nor does he provide other information that might aid in an identification. <a href="../references.html#ref-BNTH" class="source-ref">BNTHV07P413A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥibbān</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Thiqāt</span>, vol. 7 p. 413) follows al-Bukharī in distinguishing between the two, also stating that Ibn Isḥ̄q related from both. He gives no identifying information about Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allāh but states that Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥuṣayn was a “staunch faster” and among the <em>mutaʿabbīn</em> (pious slaves of God). No date of death is provided for either man. <a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV07P317B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 7 p. 317) gives his <em>kunyā</em> as “al-Taymī,” not “al-Tamīmī,” and only mentioned Ibn Isḥāq as the sole person to relate from him. Ibn Abī Ḥātim comments on the al-Bukharī ambiguity by stating that al-Bukharī mistook the latter person’s <em>ism</em> and instead of Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allāh he should be listed as Abū al-Aswad Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Nawfal al-Qarashī al-Asadī, from the <em>banu</em> Asad b. ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā (this was according to Ibn Abī Ḥātim’s father). Ibn Abī Ḥātim says that he was a slave of ʿUrwah b. al-Zubayr and was with him in Egypt during the last days of Umayyad rule of the country. He is listed as relating from several people but not al-Mujālid. If al-Mujālid died in 144/761, this would place his death some 15-20 years after the death of Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and while this is not impossible, it is unlikely that he is the possible source who is the object of our present interest. It is possible that a corruption of the <em>isnād</em> occurred where the name “Muḥammad” was added to that of Mujālid and the rest of the name for ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allāh was erased. <a href="../references.html#ref-BNKX" class="source-ref">BNKXV03P010B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥibbān</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb al-majrūḥīn min al-muḥaddithīn waʾl-ḍuʿafāʾ waʾl-matrūkīn</span>, vol. 3 p. 10) states that Mujālid had a poor memory and that his traditions should not be used as <em>fiqh</em>-ic evidence. <a href="../references.html#ref-HJKX" class="source-ref">HJKXV01P635B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muslim b. al-Ḥajjāj</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kunan waʾl-asmāʾ</span>, vol. 1 p. 635) states that he was from Kūfah and that his <em>kunyā</em> was Abū ʿUmayr and lists his primary source as al-Shaʿbī and those to whom he related as Shaʿbah a <em>mawlā</em> of ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās, Sufyān b. ʿUyaynah, and Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān. He is also mentioned as relating to ʿAbbād b. ʿAbbād al-Muhallibī (<a href="../references.html#ref-ZTTH" class="source-ref">ZTTHV03P055E</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Khaythamah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Tārīkh al-kabīr al-safar al-thālith</span>, vol. 3 p. 55)), ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAqīl al-Thaqafī (<a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV05P125C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 5 p. 125)), ʿAbd Allāh al-Ajlaḥ (<a href="../references.html#ref-BRSX" class="source-ref">BRSXV01P388C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Istīʿāb fī maʿrifat al-aṣḥāb</span>, vol. 1 p. 388)), ʿAbd Allāh b. Mubārak (<a href="../references.html#ref-JJKX" class="source-ref">JJKXV01P081D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Jurjānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kāmil fī ḍuʿafāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 1 p. 81)), ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. Ziyād (<a href="../references.html#ref-WKKH" class="source-ref">WKKHV01P109C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Khalaf al-Wakīʿ</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Akhbār al-quḍāh</span>, vol. 1 p. 109)), Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī (<a href="../references.html#ref-BNKX" class="source-ref">BNKXV02P034A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥibbān</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb al-majrūḥīn min al-muḥaddithīn waʾl-ḍuʿafāʾ waʾl-matrūkīn</span>, vol. 2 p. 34)), Abū ʿUmar al-Bazzāz (<a href="../references.html#ref-KHTG" class="source-ref">KHTGV11P144C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</span>, vol. 11 p. 144)), Abū Usāmah Ḥammād .b Usāmah (<a href="../references.html#ref-WSTX" class="source-ref">WSTXV01P207F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aslam b. Sahl al-Wāsiṭī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-wāsiṭ</span>, vol. 1 p. 207)), Asad b. ʿAmr al-Bajalī (BGHXV01P 435A), Ḥafṣ b. Ghiyāth (<a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV08P361B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 8 p. 361)), Ḥammād b. Zayd (<a href="../references.html#ref-ZTKX" class="source-ref">ZTKXV01P434A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Khaythamah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Tārīkh al-kabīr sifr al-thānī</span>, vol. 1 p. 434)), al-Haytham b. ʿAdī (<a href="../references.html#ref-KHTG" class="source-ref">KHTGV14P240R</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</span>, vol. 14 p. 240)), Hushaym b. Bashīr (<a href="../references.html#ref-BGHX" class="source-ref">BGHXV01P189A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Baghawī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Muʿjam al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 1 p. 189)), Ibrāhīm b. Sulaymān al-Muʾdib (<a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV08P361B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 8 p. 361)), Ismāʿīl b. Mujālid b. Saʿīd, his son (<a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV08P361B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 8 p. 361)), Jarīr b. Ḥāzim (one of Ibn Isḥāq’s witnesses-- <a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV08P361B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 8 p. 361)), al-Khalīl b. Zakariyā (<a href="../references.html#ref-JJKX" class="source-ref">JJKXV03P511C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Jurjānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kāmil fī ḍuʿafāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 3 p. 511)), Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Daghshī (<a href="../references.html#ref-KHTG" class="source-ref">KHTGV02P227F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</span>, vol. 2 p. 227)), Muḥammad b. Dhakwān (<a href="../references.html#ref-BGHX" class="source-ref">BGHXV04P421A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Baghawī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Muʿjam al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 4 p. 421)—although this might be an error, listing him as Mujālid b. Saʿīd b. Uqaysh), Muḥammad b. al-Ḥajjāj al-Lakhmī (<a href="../references.html#ref-KHTG" class="source-ref">KHTGV03P089C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</span>, vol. 3 p. 89)), Muḥammad b. Yazīd (<a href="../references.html#ref-WSTX" class="source-ref">WSTXV01P234F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aslam b. Sahl al-Wāsiṭī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-wāsiṭ</span>, vol. 1 p. 234)), Salamah b. Bilāl (<a href="../references.html#ref-WKKH" class="source-ref">WKKHV02P053B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Khalaf al-Wakīʿ</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Akhbār al-quḍāh</span>, vol. 2 p. 53)—in a tradition in which he mentions traveling with Ibn Isḥāq’s close traveling companion al-Ḥajjāj b. Arṭāh), Sharqī b. Qaṭṭāmī (<a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV04P376G</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 4 p. 376)), Sufyān b. Saʿīd al-Thawrī (<a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV08P361B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 8 p. 361)), al-Walīd b. al-Ḥuṣayn al-Kūfī (<a href="../references.html#ref-KHTG" class="source-ref">KHTGV15P612B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</span>, vol. 15 p. 612)), Yaḥyā b. al-Naḍr al-Buṣayr (<a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV09P192G</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 9 p. 192)), Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Bakkāʾī (<a href="../references.html#ref-KHTG" class="source-ref">KHTGV09P519B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</span>, vol. 9 p. 519)—one of Ibn Isḥāq’s well-known witnesses). Pending further evidence, it is not possible to identify the source(s) of this tradition.
[^comment-HBHXV02P114A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.
[^comment-HBHXV07P396A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. <a href="../references.html#ref-TBRB" class="source-ref">TBRBV04P268A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk (1967)</span>, vol. 4 p. 268) places the controversy over ʿUthmān&#x27;s two rakaʿah of prayer at the end of the year 29 as he does Ibn Masʿūd&#x27;s position.
[^comment-HBHXV27P071A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV27P071A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 27 p. 71) might refer to the two rakaʿah controversy. It is unclear as the passage is set in the context of Muʿawīyah&#x27;s pilgrimage during ʿUthmān&#x27;s caliphate. Not possible to establish year from context.
[^comment-HBHXV45P405C-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. It is a type of tradition that is apocalyptic in nature, referring to Yāʾjūj and Māʾjūj, often understood to be the Biblical Gog and Magog. The fragment is referred to, but not quoted without a witness in <a href="../references.html#ref-JHQX" class="source-ref">JHQXV18P235B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Qurṭubī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jāmiʿ li-aḥkām al-Qurʾān</span>, vol. 18 p. 235).References to Yāʾjūj and Māʾjūj, although not in the same form as the above, are also found in <a href="WSFAB.html" class="witness-link">WSFAB</a> (Salamah b. al-Faḍl al-Abrash al-Azraqī al-Anṣārī al-Rāzī) in Ibn Isḥāq’s discussion of Qurʾān 18:94, <a href="WYBWS.html" class="witness-link">WYBWS</a> (Yūnus b. Bukayr b. Wāṣil al-Shaybānī al-Jamāl al-Kūfī) <a href="../references.html#ref-SMJX" class="source-ref">SMJXV02P1363A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Mājah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan Ibn Majāh</span>, vol. 2 p. 1363), <a href="../references.html#ref-NSSX" class="source-ref">NSSXV02P268B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥākim al-Nīsābūrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Mustadrak ʿalā al-ṣaḥīḥīn</span>, vol. 2 p. 268), <a href="../references.html#ref-NSSX" class="source-ref">NSSXV04P535B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥākim al-Nīsābūrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Mustadrak ʿalā al-ṣaḥīḥīn</span>, vol. 4 p. 535), <a href="../references.html#ref-MYWX" class="source-ref">MYWXV02P377A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Yaʿlā Aḥmad b. ʿAlī al-Mawṣilī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 2 p. 377), <a href="../references.html#ref-MZSH" class="source-ref">MZSHV03P450F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tuḥfat al-ashrāf bi-maʿrifat al-aṭrāf</span>, vol. 3 p. 450), <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHQ" class="source-ref">KTHQV05P373B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿAẓīm</span>, vol. 5 p. 373), and <a href="../references.html#ref-AAMZ" class="source-ref">AAMZV04P199C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Abī Bakr b. Ismāʿīl al-Būṣīrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Miṣbāḥ al-zujājah fī zawāʾid Ibn Mājah</span>, vol. 4 p. 199) in reference to Qurʾān 21:96 (althoug they are not formatted in the same way). Also see <a href="WYSAU.html" class="witness-link">WYSAU</a> (Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd b. Abān al-Qurashī al-Umawī al-Kūfī) <a href="../references.html#ref-BMMX" class="source-ref">BMMXV01P306A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Amālī al-maḥāmilī</span>, vol. 1 p. 306), <a href="../references.html#ref-STJX" class="source-ref">STJXV04P155B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muʿjam al-awsaṭ</span>, vol. 4 p. 155), <a href="../references.html#ref-JJKX" class="source-ref">JJKXV07P368B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Jurjānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kāmil fī ḍuʿafāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 7 p. 368), <a href="../references.html#ref-BYTX" class="source-ref">BYTXV06P193D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm al-Thaʿlabī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Al-Kashf waʾl-bayān ʿan tafsīr al-Qurʾān</span>, vol. 6 p. 193), <a href="../references.html#ref-WHWX" class="source-ref">WHWXV03P166B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAlī b. Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Wāḥidī al-Nīsābūrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Wasīṭ fī tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-majīd</span>, vol. 3 p. 166), <a href="../references.html#ref-ANHA" class="source-ref">ANHAV01P009A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Naṣr al-Ḥasan b. Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm al-Tūnārtī al-Aṣbahānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ḥadīth Abī Naṣr al-Tūnārtī</span>, vol. 1 p. 9), <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV02P232B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 2 p. 232), <a href="../references.html#ref-JWWX" class="source-ref">JWWXV01P206B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ibn Jawzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Mawdūʿāt</span>, vol. 1 p. 206), <a href="../references.html#ref-AGAJ" class="source-ref">AGAJV01P022A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Ghanī b. ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. ̣Alī al-Maqdisī al-Jamāʿīlī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Aḥādīth al-Jamāʿīlī</span>, vol. 1 p. 22), and <a href="../references.html#ref-ZYTX" class="source-ref">ZYTXV02P311B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd Allāh b. Yūsuf b. Muḥammad al-Zaylaʿī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Takhrīj al-aḥādīth waʾl-āthār al-wāqiʿah fī tafsīr</span>, vol. 2 p. 311), but these appear to be misattributed to Muḥammad b. Isḥāq b. Yāsar and are actually related via Muḥammad b. Isḥāq al-ʿUkkāshī. In addition, they are widley considered forged. Al-Ṭabarī, in his tafsīr, states that the passage is related to Qurʾān 17:14-16, which is not discussed in the redaction of Ibn Hishām or in the al-Tabarī recension of Ibn Isḥāq’s work (see <a href="../references.html#ref-TBJB" class="source-ref">TBJBV17P105G</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Jāmiʿ al-bayān ʿan tāʾwīl āy al-Qurʾān</span>, vol. 17 p. 105)). Also see Abū al-Layth, Naṣr b. Muḥammad al-Samarqandī (<a href="../references.html#ref-LYBX" class="source-ref">LYBXV02P305D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū al-Layth</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Baḥr al-ʿulūm</span>, vol. 2 p. 305)). al-Māwardī places it in the context of the revelation of Qurʾān 21:95-97 (<a href="../references.html#ref-MATB" class="source-ref">MATBV03P471A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Māwardī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tafsīr al-Māwardī</span>, vol. 3 p. 471)). Ibn Ḥajar states that the tradition, which is well attested and with multiple <em>asānid</em>, is set in the context of a statement that Muḥammad made to his wife Zaynab after awaking from a bad dream. It is interpreted to refer to the coming breaking up of the Arabs following the murder of ʿUthmān, a kind of predictive dream of the drama to come (<a href="../references.html#ref-HJRF" class="source-ref">HJRFV13P107B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Fatḥ al-bārī sharḥ ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī</span>, vol. 13 p. 107)). There is no way to know if this is how Ibn Isḥāq understood the story. Placement is in the section following the murder of Uthmān.
[^comment-DKHXV01P379A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. A comparative passage rating the greatness of the Caliphs following Muḥammad. Appears to be the only occurance in the Ibn Isḥāq corpus. Placement is based on the type of statement usually found after the death of an individual. Notice that ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib is not mentioned. Placement is in each individual&#x27;s &quot;attributes&quot; following their deaths
[^comment-BBKHV02P035A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. The passage refers to Muʿawīyah making the pilgrimage. No date is listed. The passage in quoted in <a href="../references.html#ref-BBKH" class="source-ref">BBKHV02P035A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Isḥāq b. al-ʿAbbās al-Makkī al-Fākihī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Akhbār makkah fī qadīm al-dahr wa-ḥadīthih</span>, vol. 2 p. 35) in the chater dealing with the excellent qualities of zamzam water. Al-Ṭabarī only mentions one occasion in which Muʿawīyah took the ḥajj during his reign, that being the year 44/665 (see <a href="../references.html#ref-TBRC" class="source-ref">TBRCV01P070D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk</span>, vol. 1 p. 70)).
[^comment-HBHXV28P564A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. <a href="../references.html#ref-TBRC" class="source-ref">TBRCV05P232A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk</span>, vol. 5 p. 232) places Abū Ayyūb&#x27;s arrival in Egypt in 49, which, based on he context of <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV28P564A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 28 p. 564), must have been the context for the passage.
[^comment-HBHXV39P362A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Variations of this fragment are located in <a href="WYUAU.html" class="witness-link">WYUAU</a> (Yaʿlā b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Umayyah al-Īyādī al-Tanāfisī al-Kūfī): <a href="../references.html#ref-SHBM" class="source-ref">SHBMV03P024L</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Shaybah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kitāb al-muṣannaf fī al-aḥāddīth waʾl-āthār</span>, vol. 3 p. 24); <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī): <a href="../references.html#ref-STBX" class="source-ref">STBXV18P313C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muʿjam al-kabīr</span>, vol. 18 p. 313) and <a href="../references.html#ref-BQSX" class="source-ref">BQSXV03P576E</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 3 p. 576); <a href="WABAB.html" class="witness-link">WABAB</a> (ʿAbd al-Aʿlā b. ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Shāmī al-Baṣrī): <a href="../references.html#ref-THSH" class="source-ref">THSHV08P320A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Ṭaḥāwī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sharḥ mushkil al-āthār</span>, vol. 8 p. 320) and <a href="../references.html#ref-SHBM" class="source-ref">SHBMV03P028G</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Shaybah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kitāb al-muṣannaf fī al-aḥāddīth waʾl-āthār</span>, vol. 3 p. 28); <a href="WMUTK.html" class="witness-link">WMUTK</a> (Muḥammad b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Umayyah ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Īyādī al-Ṭanāfisī al-Kūfī): <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV39P359B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 39 p. 359); and <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī): <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV39P362A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 39 p. 362) and <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHR" class="source-ref">KTHRV07P018B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Jāmiʿ al-masānīd waʾl-sunan</span>, vol. 7 p. 18). It is a part of a series of traditions that originate from Faḍālah b. ʿUbayd, related to Ibn Isḥāq through Thumāmah b. Shufayy. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV02P177D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 2 p. 177), Abū ʿAlī Thumāmah b. Shufayy al-Hamdānī only related from a few people, including Faḍālah, ʿUqbah b. ʿĀmir, and Qubayṣah b. Dhuʾayb. He appears to have been regarded as one of the people of Egypt. <a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV02P466C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 2 p. 466) states that Thumāmah related material to Ibn Isḥāq as well as Yazīd b. Abī Ḥabīb, the source of the only clarification tradition in the group found on in the <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī) witness; all other the other traditions come to Ibn Isḥāq directly through Thumāmah. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Aḥmad b. Yūnus al-Ṣadafī, in his history of Egypt, refers to him as Thumāmah b. Shufayy al-Hamdānī, as well as al-Uḥrūjī al-Miṣrī, although what “Uḥrūj” refers to in not known. al-Ṣadafī claims that Thumāmah participated in the raid on Rhodes (Rūdas) with Faḍālah b. ʿUbayd and that he died before 120/737 during the caliphate of Hishām b. ʿAbd al-Mālik (reign c. 724-743) (see <a href="../references.html#ref-TYNX" class="source-ref">TYNXV01P080A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Aḥmad b. Yūnus al-Ṣadafī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Ibn Yūnus al-Miṣrī</span>, vol. 1 p. 80)). al-Mizzī states that Thumāmah settled in Alexandria (<a href="../references.html#ref-MZTX" class="source-ref">MZTXV04P404A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 4 p. 404)). The tradition witnessed by <a href="WYUAU.html" class="witness-link">WYUAU</a> (Yaʿlā b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Umayyah al-Īyādī al-Tanāfisī al-Kūfī) and <a href="WMUTK.html" class="witness-link">WMUTK</a> (Muḥammad b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Umayyah ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Īyādī al-Ṭanāfisī al-Kūfī) (who were brothers and likely heard the story at the same time), state that the event took place in the time of Muʿāwiyah during the invasion of “Rūm” (see <a href="../references.html#ref-SHBM" class="source-ref">SHBMV03P024L</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Shaybah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kitāb al-muṣannaf fī al-aḥāddīth waʾl-āthār</span>, vol. 3 p. 24) and <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV39P359B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 39 p. 359) respectively). <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) also states in one of the traditions he witnessed that it occurred during the invasion of “Rūm” but does not place it in a time period (see <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV39P362A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 39 p. 362)). According to Khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ, the invasion of Rhodes occurred in 59/678-679, the last year of Muʿāwīyah’s reign, under the leadership of Junādah b. Abī Umayyah (see <a href="../references.html#ref-SFTX" class="source-ref">SFTXV01P227B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ al-Shaybānī al-ʿAṣfarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh</span>, vol. 1 p. 227)). There is, however, some dispute about the year that Faḍālah b. ʿUbayd died, some placing his death in 53, others in 67. Ibn Kathīr, quoting Ibn al-Jawzī, states that Faḍālah died in 55, apparently just before the capture of Rhodes, which he covers in the following section (see <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHB" class="source-ref">KTHBV08P078B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bidāyat waʾl-nihāyah</span>, vol. 8 p. 78)). If this is accurate, the tradition may have had a foreshadowing element since it talks about death and burial just before Faḍālah’s own death. Placement should be in the year 55 or 56 under the heading of the Invasion of Rhodes.
[^comment-ZTTHV02P057A-1]: This passage is a list of people who died in Madīnah toward the end of the Caliphate of Muʿawīyah (r. 661-680CE). This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Four of the seven men listed are not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām: Khallād b. al-Sāʾib, Abū ʿUbayd-the <em>mawlā</em> of the prophet, Bashīr b. Saʿīd al-Anṣārī, and al-Ḥārith b. Ziyād. This statement is not found elsewhere in the corpus. Placement is based on content and will be placed in the section just before the death of Muʿawīyah.
[^comment-DKHXV01P379A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. A comparative passage rating the greatness of the Caliphs following Muḥammad. Appears to be the only occurance in the Ibn Isḥāq corpus. Placement is based on the type of statement usually found after the death of an individual. Notice that ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib is not mentioned. Placement is in each individual&#x27;s &quot;attributes&quot; following their deaths
[^comment-HBHXV28P70A-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV28P70A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 28 p. 70) is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Content similar to &quot;attributes&quot; genre typically following the death of the main character, in this case Muʿawīyah.
[^comment-KTHRV08P060C-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHR" class="source-ref">KTHRV08P060C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Jāmiʿ al-masānīd waʾl-sunan</span>, vol. 8 p. 60) in mentioned in reference to the biography of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Harmuz.
[^comment-ZTTHV02P212B-1]: This fragment seeks to establish the relationship between ʿUbayd Allāh al-Khawlānī’s relationship to Maymūnah. A similar fragement is also found in <a href="WABAW.html" class="witness-link">WABAW</a> (ʿAbbād b. al-ʿAwwām al-Kilābī al-Wāsiṭī), although it is worded differently and is attributed to ʿAbd Allāh al-Khawlānī not ʿUbayd al-Khawlānī. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV05P379C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 5 p. 379), he became Maymūnah&#x27;s foster son after his people left him in her care when they went out on jihād. <a href="../references.html#ref-MZTX" class="source-ref">MZTXV19P006B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 19 p. 6) gives his full name as ʿUbayd Allāh b. al-Aswad or al-Asad al-Khawlānī, but no date of death is given. <a href="../references.html#ref-MZTX" class="source-ref">MZTXV19P182D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 19 p. 182) also states that he was sometimes known as Ibn al-Aswad (there are four references to an Ibn al-Aswad in HSNX, but these are people other than al-Khawlānī). He is not mentioned in HSNX, although he is cited by <a href="WSFAB.html" class="witness-link">WSFAB</a> (Salamah b. al-Faḍl al-Abrash al-Azraqī al-Anṣārī al-Rāzī) regarding creation. There are a complex of traditions that revolve around ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib and his performance of wuḍūʿ. Although they most likely deal with the same event since ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās is the witness for each, they are sufficiently different to treat as distinct traditions. The first is refrerred to as the &quot;entering&quot; tradition, where ʿAlī enters the home of ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās and asks for water for wuḍūʿ. This tradition is found in <a href="WYWAT.html" class="witness-link">WYWAT</a> (Yaḥyā b. Wāḍiḥ al-Anṣārī Abū Tumaylah), <a href="WASKA.html" class="witness-link">WASKA</a> (ʿAbdah (ʿAbd al-Raḥmān) b. Sulaymān al-Kilābī al-Kūfī), <a href="WMSAH.html" class="witness-link">WMSAH</a> (Muḥammad b. Salamah b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Bāhilī al-Ḥarrānī), <a href="WISUL.html" class="witness-link">WISUL</a> (Ismāʿīl b. ʿUlayah), and <a href="WISIB.html" class="witness-link">WISIB</a> (Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm b. Muḥammad b. Ṭalḥah al-Ḥijāzī), <a href="WARMZ.html" class="witness-link">WARMZ</a> (ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Muḥammad b. Ziyād al-Muḥāribī al-Kūfī). The second set of traditions, where ʿAlī demonstrates how the prophet did wuḍūʿ, and it is characterized by references to ʿAlī “wiping” (مسح) himself without a stated context. This tradition is found in <a href="WYWAT.html" class="witness-link">WYWAT</a> (Yaḥyā b. Wāḍiḥ al-Anṣārī Abū Tumaylah), <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī), and <a href="WISUL.html" class="witness-link">WISUL</a> (Ismāʿīl b. ʿUlayah). The final tradition in the complex is the &quot;witness&quot; tradition in which ʿAlī describes seeing the prophet do wuḍūʿ. This tradition is found in <a href="WYWAT.html" class="witness-link">WYWAT</a> (Yaḥyā b. Wāḍiḥ al-Anṣārī Abū Tumaylah). The primary source for the fragment, Muḥammad b. Ṭalḥah b. Yazīd b. Rukānah, is cited twice in <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P565C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 565) and in <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV02P520B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 2 p. 520). He is cited several times in <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī). <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV01P120A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 1 p. 120) refers to only ʿUbayd Allāh al-Khawlān and ʿIkramah as sources and Ibn Isḥāq as a witness. See the entry for Muḥammad b. Ṭalḥah b. Yazīd b. Rukānah for more details. Placement is provisional in the section following Maymunah&#x27;s date of death, which, in <a href="WZATB.html" class="witness-link">WZATB</a> (Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ṭufayl al-Kūfī al-Bakkāʾī al-ʿĀmirī) (but not in HSNX), is listed as 63/682-683.
[^comment-WKKHV01P121A-1]: This passage is found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām and does not appear to be mentioned by other witnesses in the corpus. It gives an overview of events that led the the revolt of the people of Madīnah against Umayyad rule and the rise of Ibn Zubayr&#x27;s governors of Madīnah until their removal and the appointment of ʿAbd Allāh b. Qays b. Makhramah, a member of the family the manumitted Ibn Isḥāq’s family, after the death of Ibn Zubayr. The murder of Ismāʿīl b. Habbār b. al-Aswad al-Asadī, that sets the process in motion, is not discussed widely and no date is known. Placement is in the year 64 as the expulsion of the Umayyads and the oaths of loyalty to Ibn Zubayr seem to be the central features of the passage.
[^comment-HBHXV12P458A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām or in other sections of the . Placement is based reference to Marwān b. al-Ḥakam and his elevation to the Caliphate in Dhū al-Qaʿdah, in the year 64. See <a href="../references.html#ref-SFTX" class="source-ref">SFTXV01P253B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ al-Shaybānī al-ʿAṣfarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh</span>, vol. 1 p. 253) and p. 259A for details. This fragment is also found in an unwitnessed passage in <a href="../references.html#ref-SHBM" class="source-ref">SHBMV07P270F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Shaybah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kitāb al-muṣannaf fī al-aḥāddīth waʾl-āthār</span>, vol. 7 p. 270). Similar fragment are found in <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī) on <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV35P142B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 35 p. 142), <a href="../references.html#ref-NZDX" class="source-ref">NZDXV14P312D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Manẓūr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Mukhtaṣar Taʾrīkh Dimashq</span>, vol. 14 p. 312) (with significantly more dertails than other versions), and <a href="../references.html#ref-DHSN" class="source-ref">DHSNV13P312E</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dhahabī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Siyar aʿlām al-nubalāʾ</span>, vol. 13 p. 312).
[^comment-HJRTV14P481B-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV35P142B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 35 p. 142) (in <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī)) places this in the context of Abū Hurayrah&#x27;s sermon during the ḥajj of the year 64. Placement is based on context. Also found in <a href="WHAYA.html" class="witness-link">WHAYA</a> (Yazīd b. Hārūn al-Wāsiṭī) on <a href="../references.html#ref-AYFN" class="source-ref">AYFNV01P140A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Ṣawāf</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Fawāʾid Abū Bakr al-Naṣībī</span>, vol. 1 p. 140), <a href="../references.html#ref-NYSJ" class="source-ref">NYSJV02P091A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Nuʿaym</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṣifah al-jannah</span>, vol. 2 p. 91), <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRT" class="source-ref">HJRTV14P481B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Itḥāf al-maharah bi-al-fawāʾid al-mubtakarah min aṭrāf al-ʿasharah</span>, vol. 14 p. 481), and <a href="../references.html#ref-HJII" class="source-ref">HJIIV07P168D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Iṭrāf al-musnid al-maʿtalī bi-Iṭrāf al-musnad al-Ḥanbalī</span>, vol. 7 p. 168); as well as <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī) on <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV35P142B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 35 p. 142), <a href="../references.html#ref-NZDX" class="source-ref">NZDXV14P312D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Manẓūr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Mukhtaṣar Taʾrīkh Dimashq</span>, vol. 14 p. 312) (with significantly more dertails than other versions), and <a href="../references.html#ref-DHSN" class="source-ref">DHSNV13P312E</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dhahabī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Siyar aʿlām al-nubalāʾ</span>, vol. 13 p. 312).
[^comment-TDSHV24P175A-1]: According to <a href="../references.html#ref-TBRC" class="source-ref">TBRCV04P053A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk</span>, vol. 4 p. 53), <a href="../references.html#ref-THKX" class="source-ref">THKXV02P357A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ibn Athīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kāmil fī Taʾrīkh</span>, vol. 2 p. 357), <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV47P278A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 47 p. 278) based on the witness of Salamah b. al-Faḍl, Ibn Isḥāq places Safwan&#x27;s death in the year 19 during the conquest of al-Jazīrah. In these texts, Ibn Isḥāq includes an expanded account of the conquest, correspondence between ʿUmar and Saʿd b. Abī Waqqas, as well as the circumstances of Safwan&#x27;s death. Also see <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHB" class="source-ref">KTHBV07P076A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bidāyat waʾl-nihāyah</span>, vol. 7 p. 76), <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHB" class="source-ref">KTHBV07P096A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bidāyat waʾl-nihāyah</span>, vol. 7 p. 96), and <a href="../references.html#ref-KHDM" class="source-ref">KHDMV02P547A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Khaldūn</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Diwān al-mubtdāʾ waʾ-l-khabar fī Tārīkh al-ʿAbar waʾl-Burbur wa min ʿĀṣrahum min dhuwī al-Shāʾin al-akbar</span>, vol. 2 p. 547) that quote Ibn Isḥāq without a witness. For an Ibn Isḥāq passage witnessed by Salamah b. al-Faḍl that places Safwan&#x27;s death in the conquest of Armenia, see <a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV04P42A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 4 p. 42), <a href="../references.html#ref-BRSX" class="source-ref">BRSXV02P725A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Istīʿāb fī maʿrifat al-aṣḥāb</span>, vol. 2 p. 725), <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV24P175B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 24 p. 175). For references to Ibn Isḥāq&#x27;s account of Safwan&#x27;s death in Armenia without witness, see <a href="../references.html#ref-THRX" class="source-ref">THRXV03P031A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Athīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Usd al-ghābah fī maʿrifat al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 3 p. 31)
[^comment-TDSHV24P161A-1]: Placement is under the subject of the battel and the year because the form of the statement indicates that it refers to the cirmcumstances of Safwan&#x27;s death.
[^comment-HBHXV26P028A-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-TBRC" class="source-ref">TBRCV06P149A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk</span>, vol. 6 p. 149) places the year of ʿAbd Allāh b. Zubayr&#x27;s leading the pilgrimage as 69. Placement provisoional.
[^comment-ZTTHV01P194A-1]: This passage is found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Quotation comes from a section that focuses on Mujāhid b. Jabr, who was a regular source cited by Ibn Isḥāq. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV06P019A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 6 p. 19), his kunyā was Abū al-Ḥajjāj, and he died in 104/722. The fragment is quoted to establish his kunyā. Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj, also known as ̣Ḥumayd b. Qays al-Aʿraj was a <em>mawlā</em> of the Zubayr b. ʿAwwām family. He was a Meccan and was a specialist in Qurʾānic recitation (<a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV06P034G</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 6 p. 34)). According to <a href="../references.html#ref-BNTH" class="source-ref">BNTHV06P189D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥibbān</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Thiqāt</span>, vol. 6 p. 189), he died in Mecca in 130/747. He does not appear as a source for Ibn Isḥāq except for this passage. There are several possibilities for placement, the most likely given the structure of the text, is in the year Mujāhid b. Jabr died.
[^comment-ZTTHV02P177A-1]: This fragment is an assessment passage referring to Yazīd b. Hurmuz, who was also known as Yazīd al-Fārisī (<a href="../references.html#ref-TMSM" class="source-ref">TMSMV01P233B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Tirmidhī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Shamāʾil al-Muḥammadīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 233)) and as a <em>mawlā</em> of the <em>Banū</em> Layth. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV07P164D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 7 p. 164), Yazīd b. Hurmuz was the commander of the manumitted slaves (mawālī) at the yawm al-Ḥarah (Battle of the Camel), where he appears to have been associated with ʿUthmān&#x27;s side (<a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV08P368A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 8 p. 368)). He is often listed as the scribe for ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās (see the many passages listed below in which he writes Ibn ʿAbbās&#x27; reply to Najdah al-Ḥarūr). He is also listed as a scribe for ʿUbayd Allāh b. Ziyād (Ibid). He died during the Caliphate of ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz (c. 99/717 to 101/720--see <a href="../references.html#ref-BNTH" class="source-ref">BNTHV05P532A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥibbān</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Thiqāt</span>, vol. 5 p. 532)).He is not listed by either name in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. This assessment passage is not located elsewhere in the corpus. Yazīd b. Hurmuz is listed in the <em>isnād</em> for a fragment that deals with the role of women in battle during the raids of the prophet in <a href="WASMR.html" class="witness-link">WASMR</a> (ʿAbd al-Raḥīm b. Sulaymān al-Marwazī al-Rāzī), <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī), <a href="WMSAH.html" class="witness-link">WMSAH</a> (Muḥammad b. Salamah b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Bāhilī al-Ḥarrānī), and <a href="WHAYA.html" class="witness-link">WHAYA</a> (Yazīd b. Hārūn al-Wāsiṭī). Also see the tradition that recounts how ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb distribute charity during the Year of the Drought (Ramādah), which occurred in the year 18 during a major drought (see <a href="../references.html#ref-SFTX" class="source-ref">SFTXV01P138C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ al-Shaybānī al-ʿAṣfarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh</span>, vol. 1 p. 138)). Also see <a href="WBSAB.html" class="witness-link">WBSAB</a> (Bakr b. Sulaymān al-Aswārī al-Baṣrī), <a href="WABAW.html" class="witness-link">WABAW</a> (ʿAbbād b. al-ʿAwwām al-Kilābī al-Wāsiṭī), <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī), and <a href="WSFAB.html" class="witness-link">WSFAB</a> (Salamah b. al-Faḍl al-Abrash al-Azraqī al-Anṣārī al-Rāzī) for a reference to the event. Also see <a href="WHAYA.html" class="witness-link">WHAYA</a> (Yazīd b. Hārūn al-Wāsiṭī) and <a href="WASMR.html" class="witness-link">WASMR</a> (ʿAbd al-Raḥīm b. Sulaymān al-Marwazī al-Rāzī) for a fragment describing how Najdah al-Ḥarūrī wrote Ibn ʿAbbās about inheritance rules. The fragment is similar to the type of statement made in a death notice. Placement is provisional, based on his date of death.
[^comment-MZTXV13P190C-1]: This fragment is situated in the biography of Ṣafwān b. Sulaym and follows a discussion of his date of death. This fragment seems to be an abridged comment in which Ibn Isḥāq gave Ṣafwān&#x27;s date of death. This is an identity fragment for Ṣafwān b. Sulaym, who is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV05P417D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 5 p. 417), he was Abū ʿAbd Allāh Ṣafwān b. Sulaym a <em>mawlā</em> of Ḥumayd b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf al-Zuhrī, who died in Madīnah in 132/749, at the age of 72 (also see <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV24P137C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 24 p. 137)). He was a prolific <em>ḥadīth</em> enthusiast. <a href="../references.html#ref-TMMX" class="source-ref">TMMXV01P468A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Aḥmad al-Tamīmī al-Maghribī al-Ifrīrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Miḥan</span>, vol. 1 p. 468) lists him, along with Ibn Isḥāq, as one of the luMīnahries of Madīnah to be flogged &quot;unjustly.&quot; He relates a tradition found in <a href="WYMHA.html" class="witness-link">WYMHA</a> (Yaḥyā b. Muḥammad b. Hānīʾi) about the 99 names of God. There is no additional reference to Ṣafwān as a source. Placement is provisional for the year Ṣafwān b. Sulaym died.
[^comment-ZTTHV02P2814B-1]: This is an identity fragment for Ṣafwān b. Sulaym, who is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. See above for additional commentary.
[^comment-BKHBV05P389A-1]: Passage deals with the causes of water purity. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.
[^comment-JJKXV07P268A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content. Passage deals with the illicitness of intoxicants.
[^comment-SBDAV01P089A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content, ablutions regarding prayer. Place in ritual section after <em>Hijrah</em>.
[^comment-DRQLV08P310A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content, due to reference to albutions.
[^comment-SBDAV01P089C-1]: حدثنا سليمان بن عصام حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمر حدثنا أبي. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is approximate based on content, ablutions regarding paryer.
[^comment-HBHXV01P524B-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām or elsewhere in the corpus. The passage describes the ablution practices of ʿUthmān and how they are modeled of those of the prophet. Placement in fiqh section in ritual ablutions.
[^comment-HJRTV11P024D-1]: [] indicates the redaction of material between the tradition that the <em>isnād</em> of transmission.
[^comment-HJRTV11P027C-1]: This passage in not located in the redaction of Ibn Hishām or elsewhere in the corpus. Placement in fiqh section based on content referring the ablutions.
[^comment-DLKXV03P1167A-1]: This fragment, focusing on wiping over the ears for ablution, is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. This passage is also found in <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) and <a href="WMYKA.html" class="witness-link">WMYKA</a> (Muḥammad b. Yazīd al-Kalāʿī al-Wāsiṭī). A longer version of this fragment in found in <a href="WASKA.html" class="witness-link">WASKA</a> (ʿAbdah (ʿAbd al-Raḥmān) b. Sulaymān al-Kilābī al-Kūfī) that contains a different <em>isnād</em> (ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās to ʿUbayd Allāh al-Khawlānī to Muḥammad b. Ṭalḥah b. Yazīd to Ibn Isḥāq) and places the recollection in the context of an event, witnessed by ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās, when ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib spilled water he had planned to use for ablutions. He then recalls how both ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās had witnesses Muḥammad perform wudūʿ and the disagreements about wudūʿ that occurred after Muḥammad’s death. There is not date given and ʿAlī is not referred to as the Caliph, so it must have occurred between Muḥammad’s death in 662 and ʿAlī’s assumption of the Caliphate in 656. Lacking other information, placement will be in fiqh section under ablutions.
[^comment-HJRTV12P444A-1]: Fragment is not located in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. The passage addresses the prophet&#x27;s ritual purity practices of wiping his sacks and turban. This fragment does not appear to be found in anu other part of the corpus. Placement is in fiqh section dealing with rules of ritual purity, specifically wiping the socks and turban.
[^comment-HBHXV39P499A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām, nor is ʿUmayr the <em>mawlā</em> of ʿAbd Allāh or ʿUbayd Allāh b. ʿAbbās (for more, see below) or Abū Juhaym b. al-Ḥārith b. al-Ṣamit al-Anṣārị. Abū Juhaym&#x27;s father, al-Ḥārith b. al-Ṣamit, is mentioned four times in the redaction of Ibn Hishām but not in any context similar to the one described here. According to Ibn al-Jawzī, his <em>ism</em> was ʿĀmir (<a href="../references.html#ref-JWTX" class="source-ref">JWTXV01P196D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Jawzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Talqīḥ fuhūm ahl al-athar fī ʿuyūn al-Tārīkh waʾl-siyar</span>, vol. 1 p. 196)), while Muslim b. al-Ḥajjāj states that his <em>ism</em> was ʿAbd Allāh b. Juhaym (<a href="../references.html#ref-HJKX" class="source-ref">HJKXV01P195C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muslim b. al-Ḥajjāj</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kunan waʾl-asmāʾ</span>, vol. 1 p. 195)), and Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn al-Azdī gives it as Ḥārith b. al-Ḥārith (<a href="../references.html#ref-MHAK" class="source-ref">MHAKV01P063F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Aḥmad al-Azdī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Asmāʾ man yuʿrafu bi-kunyatihi</span>, vol. 1 p. 63)). To add to the confusion on his identity, Abū Nuʿaym says that Abū Juhaym b. al-Ḥārith b. al-Ṣamit and Abū Jahm b. al-Ḥārith b. al-Ṣamit (see below) are two different people but that there is no consensus about his actual name (<a href="../references.html#ref-NYSX" class="source-ref">NYSXV03P1611A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Nuʿaym</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Iṣbahān</span>, vol. 3 p. 1611)). In Ibn al-Athīr&#x27;s biography for Abū Juhaym b. al-Ḥārith, he states that he was a member of the Mālik b. al-Najjār clan among the <em>Anṣār</em>. His father, al-Ḥārith b. al-Ṣamit al-Anṣārị, was among the most important companions (<a href="../references.html#ref-THRX" class="source-ref">THRXV06P058A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Athīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Usd al-ghābah fī maʿrifat al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 6 p. 58)). al-Bukhārī says that Abū Juhaym was a companion (<a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV09P020G</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 9 p. 20)). Ibn Manjuwayh states that Abū Juhaym is primarily remembered for this tradition on wuḍūʾ (<a href="../references.html#ref-MRSX" class="source-ref">MRSXV01P346C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Bakr Aḥmad b. ʿAlī b. Manjuwayh</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Rijāl Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim</span>, vol. 1 p. 346)). According to al-Wāqidī, his brother, Saʿd b. al-Ḥārith, was killed supporting ʿAlī at the Battle of Ṣifīn (<a href="../references.html#ref-TBRB" class="source-ref">TBRBV11P511C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk (1967)</span>, vol. 11 p. 511)). The Biʿr Jamal (Well of the Camel) is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām either. There are several variations on this tradition in the Ibn Isḥāq/<a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) corpus. The focus on the passage is on the prophet&#x27;s practice of ritual washing. Placement in fiqh section under ritual purity.
[^comment-DKHXV02P073A-1]: The name of the well is given as Ḥamal not Jamal.
[^comment-THQXV01P106B-1]: al-Ṭaḥāwī is the only source text to mention tayyamum (see below as well).
[^comment-THSMV01P085A-1]: Note that this passage gives the hame as Abū al-Jahm b. al-Ḥārith.
[^comment-QNMXV02P187A-1]: Note that this passage gives the hame as Abū al-Jahm b. al-Ḥārith.
[^comment-QNMXV03P130A-1]: This <em>isnād</em> drops the name between ʿUbayd Allāh b. Saʿd and Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd. According to the other <em>asānid</em>, this would be Yaʿqūb b. Saʿd.
[^comment-HJRTV14P066A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām, and does not mention Abū Juhaym or Abū Juhm. This passage is significantly different from the others. <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRT" class="source-ref">HJRTV14P067C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Itḥāf al-maharah bi-al-fawāʾid al-mubtakarah min aṭrāf al-ʿasharah</span>, vol. 14 p. 67) goes on to present other <em>asānid</em> for this tradition or those like it. Those related through Ibn Isḥāq are included here. وعن العباس بن العباس بن المغيرة عن عبيد الله بن سعد عن عمه عن أبيه عن ابن إسحاق عن الأعرج نحوه وعن إسماعيل الصفار عن عباس الدوري عن عمرو الناقد عن يعقوب بن إبراهيم نحوه وعن أبي سعيد محمد ابن عبد الله بن إبراهيم المروزي عن محمد بن خلف بن عبد العزيز بن عثمان بن جبلة عن أبي حاتم أحمد بن حمدويه بن جميل بن مهران المروزي عن أبي معاذ عن أبي عصمة عن موسى بن عقبة عن الأعرج عن أبي جهيم قال أبو معاذ حدثني خارجة عن عبد الله بن عطاء عن موسى بن عقبة عن الأعرج عن أبي جهيم فذكره ولم يذكر عمير بن عبد الله رواه أحمد ثنا يعقوب ثنا أبي عن محمد بن إسحاق حدثني عبد الرحمن ابن هرمز الأعرج عن عمير مولى ابن عباس وكان ثقة عنه به وعن حسن PageV14P067 بن موسى عن ابن لهيعة عن الأعرج نحوه. PageV14P068
[^comment-TBJXV08P180A-1]: This fragment is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. There are a complex of three traditions that revolve around ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib and his performance of wuḍūʿ. Although they most likely deal with the same event since ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās is the witness for each, they are sufficiently different to treat as distinct traditions. The fragment referred to here is the “demonstration” tradition, where ʿAlī demonstrates how the prophet did wuḍūʿ, and it is characterized by references to ʿAlī “wiping” (مسح) himself without a stated context. This tradition is found in <a href="WYWAT.html" class="witness-link">WYWAT</a> (Yaḥyā b. Wāḍiḥ al-Anṣārī Abū Tumaylah), <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī), and <a href="WISUL.html" class="witness-link">WISUL</a> (Ismāʿīl b. ʿUlayah). The second tradition is referred to here as the &quot;entering&quot; tradition, where ʿAlī enters the home of ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās and asks for water for wuḍūʿ. This tradition is found in <a href="WYWAT.html" class="witness-link">WYWAT</a> (Yaḥyā b. Wāḍiḥ al-Anṣārī Abū Tumaylah), <a href="WASKA.html" class="witness-link">WASKA</a> (ʿAbdah (ʿAbd al-Raḥmān) b. Sulaymān al-Kilābī al-Kūfī), <a href="WMSAH.html" class="witness-link">WMSAH</a> (Muḥammad b. Salamah b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Bāhilī al-Ḥarrānī), <a href="WISUL.html" class="witness-link">WISUL</a> (Ismāʿīl b. ʿUlayah), and <a href="WISIB.html" class="witness-link">WISIB</a> (Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm b. Muḥammad b. Ṭalḥah al-Ḥijāzī), <a href="WARMZ.html" class="witness-link">WARMZ</a> (ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Muḥammad b. Ziyād al-Muḥāribī al-Kūfī). The final tradition in the complex is the &quot;witness&quot; tradition in which ʿAlī describes seeing the prophet do wuḍūʿ. This tradition is found in <a href="WYWAT.html" class="witness-link">WYWAT</a> (Yaḥyā b. Wāḍiḥ al-Anṣārī Abū Tumaylah).
[^comment-HBHXV43P363A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content referring to lustrations before sleep.
[^comment-SBDAV01P089B-1]: حدثنا سليمان بن عصام حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمر حدثنا أبي. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is approximate based on content, lustrations.
[^comment-BKHBV01P405A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is approximate based on content, lustrations.
[^comment-BKHBV04P300A-1]: The passage implies it is set during ʿĀʾishah&#x27;s only visit to al-Baṣrah in 36/656 although it could be when a group of women from Baṣrah, possibly on pilgrimage, visited her in Madīnah or Mecca.<a href="../references.html#ref-JHQX" class="source-ref">JHQXV08P261A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Qurṭubī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jāmiʿ li-aḥkām al-Qurʾān</span>, vol. 8 p. 261) mentions a similar tradition attributed to ʿĀʾishah but with additional <em>isnād</em> in the context of Qurʾān 9:108 that he uses to reenforce the idea of ritual purity when entering the <em>masjid</em>. <a href="../references.html#ref-ANSS" class="source-ref">ANSSV01P042A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Nasāʾī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sunan al-ṣughrā</span>, vol. 1 p. 42) refers to this variation of the tradition: أخبرنا قتيبة قال حدثنا أبو عوانة عن قتادة عن معاذة عن عائشة أنها قالت مرن أزواجكن أن يستطيبوا بالماء فإني أستحييهم منه إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يفعله. It occurs in the section on purifying with water. <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV04P300A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 4 p. 300) is the biography for al-Salt b. Muslim. al-Salt b. Muslim and Umm al-Sahbāʾ are not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-HJTT" class="source-ref">HJTTV12P452A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb</span>, vol. 12 p. 452), Umm al-Sahbāʾ was Muʿadhah <em>bint</em> ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAdawīyah al-Baṣ rīyah, the wife of Ṣāliḥ b. Ashyām. She is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām under Muʿadhah. In the witness of <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī), she is quoted by Ibn Isḥāq several times under the name Muʿadhah, see: <a href="../references.html#ref-WHNX" class="source-ref">WHNXV01P326A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAlī b. Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Wāḥidī al-Nīsābūrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Asbāb nuzūl al-Qurʾān</span>, vol. 1 p. 326) (also witnessed by <a href="WABAB.html" class="witness-link">WABAB</a> (ʿAbd al-Aʿlā b. ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Shāmī al-Baṣrī)), <a href="../references.html#ref-KTMX" class="source-ref">KTMXV01P368A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿUmar b. Shabbah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb taʾrīkh al-Madīnah al-munawwarah</span>, vol. 1 p. 368) (also witnessed by <a href="WYZAA.html" class="witness-link">WYZAA</a> (Yazīd b. Zurayʿ al-ʿAyshī al-Baṣrī)). Ibn Isḥāq also related biographical information about Umm Sahbāʾ under the name Muʿadhah <em>bint</em> ʿAbd Allāh in <a href="../references.html#ref-DRQM" class="source-ref">DRQMV02P670A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dāraquṭnī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muʾtalif waʾl-mukhtalif</span>, vol. 2 p. 670) and <a href="../references.html#ref-BRSX" class="source-ref">BRSXV04P1913C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Istīʿāb fī maʿrifat al-aṣḥāb</span>, vol. 4 p. 1913) via the witness <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī).
[^comment-HBHXV04P212B-1]: This passage is found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām or in any other witness. Deals with lustrations for Friday prayer as well as the application of scent. Placement in fiqh section under ghusl.
[^comment-ZZBXV11P116A-1]: Abū Bakr Aḥmad b. ʿAmr al-Bazzār follows this passage with the comment: &quot;وهذا الحديث بهذا اللفظ لا نعلم أحدا يرويه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا ابن عباس ولا نعلم أسند الزهري عن طاووس إلا حديثين هذا أحدهما والآخر عن ابن عمر.&quot;
[^comment-SBDAV01P092C-1]: The <em>isnād </em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is approximate based on content, spitting in the <em>masjid</em>.
[^comment-BKHBV04P044C-1]: The <em>isnād</em> drops <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) between Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm and Ibn Isḥāq. Passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. The tradition can also be found in a trucated form (as with <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV04P044C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 4 p. 44)) in <a href="WYBWS.html" class="witness-link">WYBWS</a> (Yūnus b. Bukayr b. Wāṣil al-Shaybānī al-Jamāl al-Kūfī). The passage focuses on a kind of homily about ablution, faith, and prayer. The original witness for the tradition in this complex is given four naming variations: Saʿd b. ʿUmārah, Saʿīd b. ʿUmārah, Saʿd b. ʿAmmār, and Saʿd b. ʿUbādah. Most authorities give the name as Saʿd b. ʿUmārah. Abū Nuʿaym lists his name as Saʿd b. ʿUmārah, and states that he was a companion, citing al-Bukhārī as his authority (<a href="../references.html#ref-NYMX" class="source-ref">NYMXV03P1281A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Nuʿaym</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Maʿrifat al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 3 p. 1281)). He differentiates Saʿd b. ʿUmārah, who was a member of the Saʿd b. Bakr tribe, from Saʿd b. ʿUmārah Abū Saʿīd al-Zaraqī al-Anṣārī. Ibn al-Athīr gives his name as Saʿd b. ʿUmārah al-Bakrī (<a href="../references.html#ref-THRX" class="source-ref">THRXV02P448A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Athīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Usd al-ghābah fī maʿrifat al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 2 p. 448)). Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī gives his name as Saʿd b. ʿUmārah al-Thaʿlabī and refers to this tradition (without a witness) as one of those related on his authority. Ibn Ḥajar, however, differentiates between al-Thaʿlabī and Saʿd b. ʿUmārah who was a member of the Saʿd b. Bakr. He says that Ibn Isḥāq related information from both (<a href="../references.html#ref-HJRS" class="source-ref">HJRSV03P058B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Iṣābah fī tamyīz al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 3 p. 58) to <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRS" class="source-ref">HJRSV03P059A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Iṣābah fī tamyīz al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 3 p. 59)). Ibn Ḥajar adds to the confusion in the biography of Saʿd b. Bakr, whom he says is the brother of Saʿd b. ʿUmārah (<a href="../references.html#ref-HJRS" class="source-ref">HJRSV03P210C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Iṣābah fī tamyīz al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 3 p. 210)). He says Ibn Isḥāq mentioned traditions related by both. It is not clear if Ibn Ḥajar confuses the term “aḥad” (احد-one of) with the term “akhī” (اخي-brother of). In <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV04P044C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 4 p. 44), al-Bukhārī who gives the name as Saʿd b. ʿUbādah. Ibn Saʿd lists Saʿd b. ʿUbādah b. Dulaym b. Ḥārith b. Abī Ḥazīmah b. Thaʿlabah (which may be one of the sources of Ibn Ḥajar’s confusion). Ibn Saʿd, however, places him in the Sāʿidah b. Kaʿb b. al-Khazraj tribe. He was a Madīnan companion and a frequent source for Ibn Saʿd in his <em>Ṭabaqāt</em> (<a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV03P460B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 3 p. 460)). Saʿd b. ʿUbādah is mentioned in <a href="WZATB.html" class="witness-link">WZATB</a> (Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ṭufayl al-Kūfī al-Bakkāʾī al-ʿĀmirī) as a character in at least 20 passages, but not as an eyewitness source. He is also mentioned frequently in <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī), <a href="WARMZ.html" class="witness-link">WARMZ</a> (ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Muḥammad b. Ziyād al-Muḥāribī al-Kūfī), <a href="WAIYA.html" class="witness-link">WAIYA</a> (ʿAbd Allāh b. Idrīs b. Yazīd al-Awdī al-Zaʿāfarī), <a href="WABAB.html" class="witness-link">WABAB</a> (ʿAbd al-Aʿlā b. ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Shāmī al-Baṣrī), <a href="WHAYA.html" class="witness-link">WHAYA</a> (Yazīd b. Hārūn al-Wāsiṭī), and <a href="WAANH.html" class="witness-link">WAANH</a> (ʿAbd Allāh b. Numayr al-Hamdānī al-Khāraqī al-Kūfī) as both a source and a character.
[^comment-THRXV02P448A-1]: The <em>isnād</em> drops <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) between Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm and Ibn Isḥāq.
[^comment-SBDAV01P092D-1]: The <em>isnād </em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is approximate based on content, prayer positions.
[^comment-SBDAV01P090D-1]: The <em>isnād </em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. The context of the passage refers to talking during prayer and is after the return from Abyssinia but contrasting the pre and post immigration practice of prayer.
[^comment-SBDAV01P093E-1]: The <em>isnād </em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Context deals with talking while in prayer.
[^comment-SBDAV01P092F-1]: The <em>isnād</em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Passage deals with the arrangemebnt of rows for prayer.
[^comment-ZTTHV01P173A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Refers to the original command to perform two stanzas of prayer that were then increased to four.
[^comment-SBDAV01P090E-1]: The <em>isnād</em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. The context of this passage, which refers to the recitation of two ʿayāt from Qurʾān 2, must come after the completion of Surat al-Baqra.
[^comment-SBDAV01P097B-1]: the <em>ḥadīth</em> that follow use the <em>isnād</em> from Ibn Isḥāq as follows: حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثنا أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Passage deals with the actions of the Imām before the taslīm.
[^comment-SBDAV01P092B-1]: The <em>isnād</em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Refers to the taslīm at the end of the ṣalāt.
[^comment-SBDAV01P093A-1]: The <em>isnād</em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Deals with timing of prayer.
[^comment-DWNXV02P025A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. The passage concerns the prophet&#x27;s prayer practices that were forbidden to others. Does not appear to be found in any other witness in the corpus. Placement is based on content and in the fiqh section under prayer.
[^comment-HBHXV37P409A-1]: This refers to an event apparently late in Muḥammad&#x27;s life when it became difficult for him to complete the recitation of the prayer. It is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām, nor is the phrase &quot;Umm al-Qur&#x27;an.&quot; This represents one of Ibn Isḥāq&#x27;s most frequently reused passages. Placement is based on content dealing with prayer. The passage is also found in <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b.
