Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī): <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV37P409A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Numayr al-Hamdānī al-Khāraqī al-Kūfī): <a href="../references.html#ref-BRWX" class="source-ref">BRWXV11P044C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Tamhīd li-mā fī al-Muwaṭṭāʾ min al-maʿānī waʾl-asānīd</span>, vol. 11 p. 44), <a href="../references.html#ref-BNHX" class="source-ref">BNHXV05P095A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥibbān</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Iḥsān fī taqrīb Ṣaḥīḥ Ibn Ḥibbān</span>, vol. 5 p. 95), <a href="../references.html#ref-BQQX" class="source-ref">BQQXV01P056C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb al-qurāʾ khalaf al-imām</span>, vol. 1 p. 56), <a href="../references.html#ref-BRWX" class="source-ref">BRWXV11P044A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Tamhīd li-mā fī al-Muwaṭṭāʾ min al-maʿānī waʾl-asānīd</span>, vol. 11 p. 44), <a href="../references.html#ref-TTXX" class="source-ref">TTXXV02P222C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad b. Aḥmad b. ʿAbd al-Hādī al-Ḥanbalī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tanqīḥ al-taḥqīq</span>, vol. 2 p. 222), <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRT" class="source-ref">HJRTV06P424B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Itḥāf al-maharah bi-al-fawāʾid al-mubtakarah min aṭrāf al-ʿasharah</span>, vol. 6 p. 424); <a href="WUMHA.html" class="witness-link">WUMHA</a> (ʿUmar b. Ḥabīb): <a href="../references.html#ref-DRQS" class="source-ref">DRQSV02P099A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dāraquṭnī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-Dāraquṭnī</span>, vol. 2 p. 99), <a href="../references.html#ref-BQQX" class="source-ref">BQQXV01P056C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb al-qurāʾ khalaf al-imām</span>, vol. 1 p. 56), <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRT" class="source-ref">HJRTV06P424B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Itḥāf al-maharah bi-al-fawāʾid al-mubtakarah min aṭrāf al-ʿasharah</span>, vol. 6 p. 424); <a href="WISUL.html" class="witness-link">WISUL</a> (Ismāʿīl b. ʿUlayah): <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRT" class="source-ref">HJRTV06P424B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Itḥāf al-maharah bi-al-fawāʾid al-mubtakarah min aṭrāf al-ʿasharah</span>, vol. 6 p. 424); <a href="WYAHA.html" class="witness-link">WYAHA</a> (Yazīd b. Abī Ḥabīb (Suwayd) al-Azdī al-Miṣrī): <a href="../references.html#ref-BQQX" class="source-ref">BQQXV01P056C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb al-qurāʾ khalaf al-imām</span>, vol. 1 p. 56); <a href="WHSDB.html" class="witness-link">WHSDB</a> (Ḥammād b. Salamah b. Dīnār al-Baṣrī): <a href="../references.html#ref-BQQX" class="source-ref">BQQXV01P056C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb al-qurāʾ khalaf al-imām</span>, vol. 1 p. 56); and without a witness: <a href="../references.html#ref-IHMA" class="source-ref">IHMAV02P271A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥāzim</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muḥallā bil-Āthār</span>, vol. 2 p. 271) and <a href="../references.html#ref-BQQX" class="source-ref">BQQXV01P064B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb al-qurāʾ khalaf al-imām</span>, vol. 1 p. 64).
[^comment-HJRTV06P424B-1]: According to Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī (d. 463), he was one of the memorizers of <em>ḥadīth</em> who traveled in search of new traditions. Ibn Isḥāq is not listed in the <em>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</em> as relating to him. He was born in 228 and began to write traditions down at in the year 239 (<a href="../references.html#ref-KHTG" class="source-ref">KHTGV16P341A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</span>, vol. 16 p. 341)), writing 5 or 6 volumes. Since Ibn Isḥāq died at the latest in 159 there is no way Yaḥyā b. Ṣāʿid could have related directly from him. Where listed as relating from Ibn Isḥāq, there must be a link or two missing. He is not listed by Khaṭīb as relating from any of Ibn Isḥāq’s witnesses. According to Ibn ʿAsākir, he did hear from Saʿīd b. Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd al-Umawī, the son of the witness Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd al-Umawī (<a href="WYSAU.html" class="witness-link">WYSAU</a> (Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd b. Abān al-Qurashī al-Umawī al-Kūfī)) in Iraq (<a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV64P357A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 64 p. 357)). There is reason to think that the Ibn Isḥāq listed in <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRT" class="source-ref">HJRTV06P424B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Itḥāf al-maharah bi-al-fawāʾid al-mubtakarah min aṭrāf al-ʿasharah</span>, vol. 6 p. 424) is actually Muḥammad b. Isḥāq b. Khuzaymah (see, for instance, <a href="../references.html#ref-TLBX" class="source-ref">TLBXV07P3373B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-ʿAdīm</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Bughyat al-ṭalab fī taʾrīkh Ḥalab</span>, vol. 7 p. 3373)). In the <em>isnād</em> found in <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRT" class="source-ref">HJRTV06P424B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Itḥāf al-maharah bi-al-fawāʾid al-mubtakarah min aṭrāf al-ʿasharah</span>, vol. 6 p. 424) that lists Ibn Isḥāq as relating to Yaḥyā b. Ṣāʿid, Ibn Isḥāq’s source was ʿAbd Allāh b. Yūsuf al-Tunīsī, who was not one of our Ibn Isḥāq’s sources. The other possible source listed, is Ibn Abī Farwah, or Isḥāq b. Abī Farwah who could be one of several individuals, is not listed anywhere as a source for Ibn Isḥāq. In the above passage, and also in <a href="../references.html#ref-DRQS" class="source-ref">DRQSV02P099C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dāraquṭnī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-Dāraquṭnī</span>, vol. 2 p. 99), <a href="../references.html#ref-BQSX" class="source-ref">BQSXV02P234C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 2 p. 234), and <a href="../references.html#ref-BQQX" class="source-ref">BQQXV01P056C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb al-qurāʾ khalaf al-imām</span>, vol. 1 p. 56), Ibn Ṣāʿid is listed as relating from ʿUbayd Allāh b. Saʿd, the grandson of <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī). It is therefore possible that there are several links between Ibn Isḥāq and Ibn Ṣāʿid. It is this lack of clarity that Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī seeks to clarify.
[^comment-HBHXV39P444A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Passage refers to the morning prayer and the witr prayer. The phrase &quot;حمر النعم&quot; occurs in <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV1P135A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 135) in reference to the &quot;حلف الفضول.&quot;
[^comment-HBHXV43P376A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Set in the context of a recollection of a comment from ʿĀʾishah during the Caliphate of ʿUmar that she sleep in front of the prophet while he prayed. ʿUrwah b. al-Zubayr appears to have mentioned the tradition to Abū Umāmah b. Sahl, who objected to the recollection. ʿUrwah, however, compared it to the funeral prayer. Also mentioned the witr prayer. The tradition of whether ʿĀʾishah layed between the prophet and the <em>qiblah</em> seems to have been witnessed only by <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī).
[^comment-KHLSV03P266B-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. <a href="../references.html#ref-KHLS" class="source-ref">KHLSV03P266B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-ʿAbbās al-Baghdādī al-Mukhalliṣ</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Al-Mukhalliṣīyāt wa-ajaziʾ akhrā</span>, vol. 3 p. 266) is similar to <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV43P376A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 43 p. 376) but it does not mention ʿUmar or the context of recollection. Mentions that ʿĀʾishah would sleep between the prophet and the <em>qiblah</em> during prayer. Also mentioned the witr prayer.The tradition of whether ʿĀʾishah layed between the prophet and the <em>qiblah</em> seems to have been witnessed only by <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī).
[^comment-HBHXV23P157A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. The fragment discusses the rules of purity in facing the <em>qiblah</em> and an apparent contradiction in prohibitions. A similar passage with slightly different phrasing is also found in <a href="WJHZA.html" class="witness-link">WJHZA</a> (Jarīr b. Ḥāzim b. Zayd b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Shajāʿ al-Azdī al-ʿAtkī al-Baṣrī). Placement in fiqh section under prayer practices.
[^comment-NSSXV01P257A-1]: The <em>isnād</em> mistakenly lists Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm b. Saʿīd instead of Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd.
[^comment-MMUHV01P037B-1]: The <em>isnād</em> appears to drop Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd. and to refer to Abū Isḥāq instead of Ibn Isḥāq.
[^comment-SBDAV01P092A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Refers to praying infront of a mirror. The <em>isnād </em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن.
[^comment-BKHTV01P522A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām and appears to be the only witness to the story in the Ibn Isḥāq corpus. The passage refers to Muḥammad’s practice of doing sujūd when reciting Qurʾān 84:1. Abū Ibrāhīm or Abū ʿUthmān Muḥammad b. Qays al-Madinī al-Zayāt, A <em>mawlā</em> of Yaʿqūb al-Qibṭī, is not mentioned as an informant in the redaction of Ibn Hishām It is interesting to note that Ibn Qays is described here as a “storyteller.” The context of Ibn Qays hearing the tradition was when he was telling stories to ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, when ʿUmar was governor of Madīnah. According to Ibn Qutaybah, ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz was appointed governor of Madīnah in the year 86/705 and served for seven years and five months, or until 94/712 (<a href="../references.html#ref-QKMX" class="source-ref">QKMXV01P359B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Qutaybah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb al-maʿārif</span>, vol. 1 p. 359)). Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sakāwī, Ibn Qays died in Madīnah during the fitnah of al-Walīd b. Yazīd (<a href="../references.html#ref-MSTM" class="source-ref">MSTMV02P569B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sakāwī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Al-Tuḥfat al-laṭifat fī taʾrīkh al-Madīnat al-Sharīfat</span>, vol. 2 p. 569)), which occured in 126/743 (this event killed many <em>ḥadīth</em> enthusiasts and prominent Madīnans, see <a href="../references.html#ref-TKHL" class="source-ref">TKHLV01P421H</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ al-Shaybānī al-ʿAṣfarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ</span>, vol. 1 p. 421)). Abū Salamah b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf b. ʿAbd ʿAwf b. al-Ḥārith is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishāmin any <em>isnād</em>. According to Ibn Saʿd, he died in 94/712 or 104/722 (<a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV05P120B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 5 p. 120)) and collected traditions from Abū Hurayrah (see <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV04P252A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 4 p. 252)). Placement is in section referring to the prophet&#x27;s practices in prayer.
[^comment-BKHBV01P213A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV01P213A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 1 p. 213) is mentioned in the biography of Muḥammad b. Qays which depicts Ibn Qays as a confidant ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.
[^comment-SBDAV01P091A-1]: The <em>isnād </em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Refers to group prayer. Most likely after the <em>hijrah</em>.
[^comment-SBDAV01P091B-1]: The <em>isnād </em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. The pasage is truncated andf refers to group prayer. Most likely after the <em>hijrah</em>.
[^comment-SBDAV01P090C-1]: The <em>isnād </em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Refers to the order of the Friday sermon and prayer.
[^comment-BQSXV02P204A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Note that the <em>isnād</em> found in <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) on <a href="../references.html#ref-BQSX" class="source-ref">BQSXV02P204A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 2 p. 204) begins with ʿĀʾishah but similar fragments that also examine the <em>tashahhud</em> prayer, with a different formula, is eye-witnessed by ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd and provided to Ibn Isḥāq by ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Aswad in <a href="WABAB.html" class="witness-link">WABAB</a> (ʿAbd al-Aʿlā b. ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Shāmī al-Baṣrī) on <a href="../references.html#ref-TBTD" class="source-ref">TBTDV01P323B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-athār</span>, vol. 1 p. 323) and <a href="../references.html#ref-KHZX" class="source-ref">KHZXV01P349A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Khuzaymah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Saḥīḥ</span>, vol. 1 p. 349). <a href="../references.html#ref-ASHD" class="source-ref">ASHDV04P271C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-ʿAynī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sharḥ Sunan Abī Dāwūd</span>, vol. 4 p. 271) states that Ibn Isḥāq also related a tradition sourced from ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd via <a href="WYBWS.html" class="witness-link">WYBWS</a> (Yūnus b. Bukayr b. Wāṣil al-Shaybānī al-Jamāl al-Kūfī), but he does not provide a quotation. <a href="../references.html#ref-HJII" class="source-ref">HJIIV04P129C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Iṭrāf al-musnid al-maʿtalī bi-Iṭrāf al-musnad al-Ḥanbalī</span>, vol. 4 p. 129) lists a fragment via <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) eye-witnessed by ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd, and provided to Ibn Isḥāq by ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Aswad, but does not mention other traditions, such as that sourced by Ibn Isḥāq from ʿĀʾishah. An unwitnessed fragment is also found on <a href="../references.html#ref-BQSX" class="source-ref">BQSXV02P203A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 2 p. 203).
[^comment-BQSXV02P205C-1]: This fragment is sourced from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd al-Qārī and not ʿĀʾishah. It is therefore a different tradition and while belonging to the broad <em>tashahhud</em> prayer category, it is not a variation of the passage above.
[^comment-SBDAV01P093B-1]: The <em>isnād </em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Deals with prayer rituals at funerals.
[^comment-JJKXV03P319A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Refers to the prayer for a solar eclipse. Not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām
[^comment-SBDAV01P092C-1]: The <em>isnād </em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Passage deals with Ṣadaqah. Might also be placed in biography of al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī.
[^comment-SBDAV01P092E-1]: The <em>isnād </em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Appears to refer to fasting during Ramadan.
[^comment-SBDAV01P097C-1]: the hadith that follow use the <em>isnād </em> from Ibn Isḥāq as follows: حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثنا أبي عن. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Passage refers to the sighting of the moon to mark the ending of fasting.

Versions of this passage also found in <a href="WASKA.html" class="witness-link">WASKA</a> (ʿAbdah (ʿAbd al-Raḥmān) b. Sulaymān al-Kilābī al-Kūfī) and <a href="WMSAH.html" class="witness-link">WMSAH</a> (Muḥammad b. Salamah b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Bāhilī al-Ḥarrānī).
[^comment-ANSSV04P200A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.
[^comment-MZSHV12P359A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.
[^comment-HJIIV09P273A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.
[^comment-HBHXV39P385A-1]: This is part of a series of traditions that appear to originate with Faḍālah b. ʿUbayd that discuss vomiting and its impact on the status of fasting. In this series there is a great deal of variation, but most suggest that Faḍālah was with the prophet and when someone offered him a drink or when he asked for a drink, Muḥammad was asked about the status of his fast. He replies generally that he was had been fasting but then vomited and was no longer fasting. In some traditions in the series there are comments about whether vomiting “breaks” the fast or if Muḥammad chose to end his fast after vomiting. There appears to be some dispute in the legal tradition about vomiting and its impact on the status of the fast, which these traditions address. The fragments are not separated into specific style types and are simply group by subject. They are witnessed by <a href="WHSDB.html" class="witness-link">WHSDB</a> (Ḥammād b. Salamah b. Dīnār al-Baṣrī): <a href="../references.html#ref-THSH" class="source-ref">THSHV04P379A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Ṭaḥāwī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sharḥ mushkil al-āthār</span>, vol. 4 p. 379), <a href="../references.html#ref-THSM" class="source-ref">THSMV02P096D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Ṭaḥāwī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sharḥ maʿānī al-āthār</span>, vol. 2 p. 96), <a href="../references.html#ref-RZZI" class="source-ref">RZZIV03P063B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-ʿIlal</span>, vol. 3 p. 63), <a href="../references.html#ref-STBX" class="source-ref">STBXV18P316B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muʿjam al-kabīr</span>, vol. 18 p. 316), <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV12P036D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 12 p. 36), <a href="../references.html#ref-MZSH" class="source-ref">MZSHV08P263C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tuḥfat al-ashrāf bi-maʿrifat al-aṭrāf</span>, vol. 8 p. 263), <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHR" class="source-ref">KTHRV07P020A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Jāmiʿ al-masānīd waʾl-sunan</span>, vol. 7 p. 20), <a href="../references.html#ref-AAMZ" class="source-ref">AAMZV02P066A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Abī Bakr b. Ismāʿīl al-Būṣīrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Miṣbāḥ al-zujājah fī zawāʾid Ibn Mājah</span>, vol. 2 p. 66), and <a href="../references.html#ref-YNQX" class="source-ref">YNQXV11P036B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-ʿAynī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>ʿUmdat al-qārī sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī</span>, vol. 11 p. 36); <a href="WYUAU.html" class="witness-link">WYUAU</a> (Yaʿlā b. ʿUbayd b. Passage deals with fasting while traveling. Passage also found in <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī), <a href="WYSAU.html" class="witness-link">WYSAU</a> (Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd b. [^comment-HBHXV04P195A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. or in any other part of the corpus. Placement in the fiqh section on marriage.
[^comment-HBHXV44P181A-1]: Placed in post-<em>hijrah</em> ritual section. Not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām.
[^comment-HBAIV01P081A-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-HBAI" class="source-ref">HBAIV01P081A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAlī b. al-Madīnī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-ʿIlal</span>, vol. 1 p. 81) states that the tradition is &quot;wrong&quot; (وهذا غلط). The correct <em>isnād </em> is: ورواه يحيى بن سعيد عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عبد الله بن الزبير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم. Placement is based on <a href="../references.html#ref-NSKX" class="source-ref">NSKXV05P201A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Nasāʾī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 5 p. 201). Not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām.
[^comment-NSKXV05P201A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content. <a href="../references.html#ref-BQMX" class="source-ref">BQMXV11P258A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Maʿrifat al-sunan waʾl-āthār</span>, vol. 11 p. 258) attributes a similar tradition to Ibn Isḥāq without a witness and in the following passage states that the &quot;same&quot; tradition was related via Jarīr, probably Ibn Ḥāzim (<a href="WJHZA.html" class="witness-link">WJHZA</a> (Jarīr b. Ḥāzim b. Zayd b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Shajāʿ al-Azdī al-ʿAtkī al-Baṣrī)).
[^comment-HJRQV05P077A-1]: This passage is found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Provisional placement in fiqh section under marriage. Deals with the issue of the loss of a women&#x27;s hair and the revelation of Qurʾān 24:31. This appears to be the only Ibn Isḥāq passage that specifically discusses this verse. That it is found in Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī seems odd given the late date of the author. Similar passages are also found in <a href="WMSAH.html" class="witness-link">WMSAH</a> (Muḥammad b. Salamah b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Bāhilī al-Ḥarrānī), <a href="WJHZA.html" class="witness-link">WJHZA</a> (Jarīr b. Ḥāzim b. Zayd b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Shajāʿ al-Azdī al-ʿAtkī al-Baṣrī), <a href="WASKA.html" class="witness-link">WASKA</a> (ʿAbdah (ʿAbd al-Raḥmān) b. Sulaymān al-Kilābī al-Kūfī), <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī), and <a href="WJHZA.html" class="witness-link">WJHZA</a> (Jarīr b. Ḥāzim b. Zayd b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Shajāʿ al-Azdī al-ʿAtkī al-Baṣrī) but do not refer to the same back story or refer to any Qurʾānic verse as a foundation. <a href="WJHZA.html" class="witness-link">WJHZA</a> (Jarīr b. Ḥāzim b. Zayd b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Shajāʿ al-Azdī al-ʿAtkī al-Baṣrī), <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī), <a href="WASKA.html" class="witness-link">WASKA</a> (ʿAbdah (ʿAbd al-Raḥmān) b. Sulaymān al-Kilābī al-Kūfī), and <a href="WYUAU.html" class="witness-link">WYUAU</a> (Yaʿlā b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Umayyah al-Īyādī al-Tanāfisī al-Kūfī) gives the witness as Asmā <em>bint</em> Abī Bakr not ʿĀʾishah.
[^comment-MNHSV01P079B-1]: Passage discusses marriage regulations between neices and nephews and aunts and uncles. Not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Similar passage also found in <a href="WASKA.html" class="witness-link">WASKA</a> (ʿAbdah (ʿAbd al-Raḥmān) b. Sulaymān al-Kilābī al-Kūfī). Placement in fiqh section under marriage.
[^comment-BKHBV01P171C-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. The tradition is set during the ḥajj when ʿAdī b. ʿAdī al-Kindī advised Muḥammad b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Ṣāliḥ al-Makkī to go collect a tradition from Ṣafīyah <em>bint</em> Shaybah b. ʿUthmān b. Abī Ṭalḥah. Muḥammad b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Ṣāliḥ and ʿAdī b. ʿAdī al-Kindī are not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām Ṣafīyah <em>bint</em> Shaybah b. ʿUthmān is mentioned in <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV02P411C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 2 p. 411) regarding the Conquest of Mecca (also see via <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) <a href="../references.html#ref-NYMX" class="source-ref">NYMXV06P3378A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Nuʿaym</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Maʿrifat al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 6 p. 3378)). Thawr b. Yazīd al-Kalāʿī, Abū Khālid, is mentioned three times by <a href="WZATB.html" class="witness-link">WZATB</a> (Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ṭufayl al-Kūfī al-Bakkāʾī al-ʿĀmirī) (<a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P166A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 166), <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P308A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 308), and <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P634C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 634)). According to Muḥammad b. Saʿd, he was from the people of Ḥimṣ and died in Jerusalem in 153/770 at the age of 60. His grandfather fought for Muʿāwiyah at Ṣiffīn against ʿAlī (<a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV07P324A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 7 p. 324)). Muḥammad b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Ṣāliḥ al-Makkī is mentioned in <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV01P171C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 1 p. 171), <a href="../references.html#ref-HJKX" class="source-ref">HJKXV01P583A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muslim b. al-Ḥajjāj</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kunan waʾl-asmāʾ</span>, vol. 1 p. 583), <a href="../references.html#ref-BNTH" class="source-ref">BNTHV07P371C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥibbān</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Thiqāt</span>, vol. 7 p. 371), and <a href="../references.html#ref-MZTX" class="source-ref">MZTXV19P215A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 19 p. 215) only in relation to this tradition, although the latter source states that he also related from Mujāhid b. Jabr al-Makkī and in addition to Thawr b. Yazīd al-Ḥimṣī, he also related to Mujāhid b. Jabr al-Makkī. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRB" class="source-ref">HJRBV09P330A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb</span>, vol. 9 p. 330) he lived in Jerusalem. No date of death is mentioned. ʿAdī b. ʿAdī b. ʿUmayrah al-Kindī al-Shaybānī, Abū Farwah al-Jazīrī, was a member of the al-Ḥārith b. Muʿāwiyah b. Thawr tribe. Described as pious by al-Ṭabarī, he commanded troops under Muḥammad b. Marwān against Khārijī rebels in 76/ 695 (<a href="../references.html#ref-TBRB" class="source-ref">TBRBV06P243A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk (1967)</span>, vol. 6 p. 243)). He is described as a partisan of the Umayyads and was appointed as commander of Mūsil, the Jazīrah, and then Armīnīyah by ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz (<a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV40P137A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 40 p. 137), although <a href="../references.html#ref-MZTX" class="source-ref">MZTXV19P5354B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 19 p. 5354) states this was done by Sulaymān b. ʿAbd al-Mālik). He was included among the 3rd generation of successors in the Jazīrah and to have been trustworthy (ibid., 138). He died in 120/738 according to al-Dhahabī and others (<a href="../references.html#ref-DHBR" class="source-ref">DHBRV01P116D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dhahabī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-ʿIbar fī khabar man ghabar</span>, vol. 1 p. 116)). Ṣafīyah <em>bint</em> Shaybah b. ʿUthmān b. Abī Ṭalḥah was a Meccan companion and related from many of the Prophet&#x27;s wives and related to many in the first generation of successors. No date of death is mentioned (see, <a href="../references.html#ref-MZTX" class="source-ref">MZTXV35P212B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 35 p. 212)). One of the most comonly quoted traditions in the Ibn Isḥāq corpus. Passage also found in <a href="WAANH.html" class="witness-link">WAANH</a> (ʿAbd Allāh b. Numayr al-Hamdānī al-Khāraqī al-Kūfī), <a href="WZAZA.html" class="witness-link">WZAZA</a> (Zakarīyā b. Abī Zāʾidah), and <a href="WASMR.html" class="witness-link">WASMR</a> (ʿAbd al-Raḥīm b. Sulaymān al-Marwazī al-Rāzī). Unable to place the date of the event in which the tradition was collected in Mecca. Most likely to be placed in the opinions of Muḥammad in fiqh section.
[^comment-NSKXV07P027A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Deals with punishments for stealing. Similar passages are also found in <a href="WABAB.html" class="witness-link">WABAB</a> (ʿAbd al-Aʿlā b. ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Shāmī al-Baṣrī), <a href="WMSAH.html" class="witness-link">WMSAH</a> (Muḥammad b. Salamah b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Bāhilī al-Ḥarrānī), and <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī), which places the value at ten dirhāms (also see <a href="../references.html#ref-YNQX" class="source-ref">YNQXV23P279C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-ʿAynī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>ʿUmdat al-qārī sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī</span>, vol. 23 p. 279) witnessed by <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī)). Passage provisionally placed in fiqh section under ḥadd punishments.
[^comment-HBHXV01P260A-1]: Ibn Mājdah is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām.
[^comment-SBDAV01P093D-1]: The <em>isnād </em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV01P227A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 1 p. 227) the prophet&#x27;s reply that is missing from this tradition is: قل اللهم عالم الغيب والشهادة فاطر السماوات والأرض رب كل شيء ومليكه أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت أعوذ بك من شر نفسي ومن شر الشيطان وشركه وأمره أن يقوله إذا أصبح وإذا أمسى وإذا أخذ مضجعه. Context is not clear and it is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Might be placed in section following Abū Bakr&#x27;s death.
[^comment-BMMXV01P073A-1]: Abū Jarrāḥ is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.
[^comment-MGHSV01P1031B-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-MGHS" class="source-ref">MGHSV01P1031B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Mughalṭāy b. Qalīj</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sharḥ sunan Ibn Mājah</span>, vol. 1 p. 1031) omits <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) from the <em>isnād</em>.
[^comment-HBHXV43P360A-1]: The passage in <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV43P360A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 43 p. 360) and its variants is placed here due to subject being Abū Rāfiʿ and his wife Salamah. Hārūn al-Wāsiṭī). Abū Qatādah is mentioned over 80 times in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.

Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 459). It is the only reference to Abū Masʿūd in the redaction of Ibn Hishām.

Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 586), vol. 1, 642A, and vol. 2, 651A. He is also mentioned as a participant in the narrative in vol. 2, 301A, vol. 2, 348A, vol. 2, 353A, vol. 2, 443A, vol. 2, 606A, vol. 2, 622A, vol. 2, 623A, vol. 2, 641A, and vol. 2, 662A. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām.
[^comment-SBDAV01P090A-1]: Placment based on content, regarding prayer. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. The eyewitness, Abū Saʿīd al-Khadrī, or Saʿd b. Mālik b. Sinān b. ʿUbayd b. Thaʿlabah (see <a href="../references.html#ref-TKHL" class="source-ref">TKHLV01P166A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ al-Shaybānī al-ʿAṣfarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ</span>, vol. 1 p. 166)) was a popular source for Ibn Isḥāq . He died in 74/692-963. Although too young to participate in the early battles, Abū Saʿīd took part in 12 expoditions during Muḥammad&#x27;s life (see, <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRB" class="source-ref">HJRBV03P479A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb</span>, vol. 3 p. 479)).
[^comment-BQSXV02P479A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.
[^comment-BQSXV02P479B-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content. <a href="../references.html#ref-BQSX" class="source-ref">BQSXV02P479A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 2 p. 479) and <a href="../references.html#ref-BQSX" class="source-ref">BQSXV02P479B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 2 p. 479) seem to refer to the role of the call to prayer in driving Shaytān from the <em>masjid</em>. Placement provisional and may be better placed in section on prayer or on the call to prayer.
[^comment-HBHXV15P078A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content. <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV15P78A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 15 p. 78) seems to be evaluative of two of Abū Hurayrah&#x27;s common transmitters Khubayb b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Hafṣ b. ʿĀsim. Similar evaluative traditions are found in the biographies of Maʿbad b. Kaʿb (see <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV37P291A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 37 p. 291))and Muḥammad b. Muslim b. Shihāb al-Zuhrī (see <a href="../references.html#ref-MYWX" class="source-ref">MYWXV13P408A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Yaʿlā Aḥmad b. ʿAlī al-Mawṣilī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 13 p. 408)). Abū Hurayrah is mentioned only in <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV02P656A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 2 p. 656).
[^comment-SBDAV01P090B-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. The <em>isnād</em> before Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. The content of the passage regards the correctness of raising the head before the imām during prayer. No other example of this or a similar tradition has been located from Ibn Isḥāq .
[^comment-ZTTHV03P063A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. It is drawn from Ibn Abī Khaythamah’s biography of al-Aswad b. Yazīd, the father of Ibn Isḥāq’s source, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Aswad. The passage is meant to establish the relationship between al-Aswad b. Yazīd, his uncle ʿAlqamah b. Qays b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Nakhaʿī, and ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb. Since ʿAlqamah was closely associated with ʿAlī, and fought on his side at Ṣiffīn, it is also designed to show that he and al-Aswad were a part of the mainstream. No date is given for the scene and the passage will be placed in the biographical section for both ʿal-Aswad and ʿAlqamah.
[^comment-ZTTHV03P065A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. It is drawn from Ibn Abī Khaythamah’s biography of al-Aswad b. Yazīd, the father of Ibn Isḥāq’s source, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Aswad. The passage is meant to establish his relationship with ʿĀʾishah. The term “<em>bi-makān</em>” means “a place” and is occasionally used to denote an unknown location (see, for instance, <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P616C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 616)). This appears to be the only instance of this fragment in the Ibn Isḥāq corpus.
[^comment-BKHBV02P047A-1]: In the witness of Salamah b. al-Faḍl, there is an analogous passage but with more detail that includes the story of how ʿAbbād b. Bishr killed Kaʿb b. al-Ashrāf al-Yahūdī, along with a poem of praise, see <a href="../references.html#ref-BRSX" class="source-ref">BRSXV02P802B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Istīʿāb fī maʿrifat al-aṣḥāb</span>, vol. 2 p. 802) to <a href="../references.html#ref-BRSX" class="source-ref">BRSXV02P804A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Istīʿāb fī maʿrifat al-aṣḥāb</span>, vol. 2 p. 804) (<a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV02P276A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 2 p. 276) states that ʿAbd Allāh b. Unays killed Kaʿb b. al-Ashrāf and includes a different poem of praise). For an quotation of a similar passage without a withness, see <a href="../references.html#ref-DHTI" class="source-ref">DHTIV03P207A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dhahabī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-Islām</span>, vol. 3 p. 207), <a href="../references.html#ref-MZTX" class="source-ref">MZTXV03P249A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 3 p. 249), <a href="../references.html#ref-MZTX" class="source-ref">MZTXV14P105A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 14 p. 105). This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām.
[^comment-TDSHV09P080A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Also via these <em>asānid</em> in <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV09P080A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 9 p. 80): وأخبرنا أبو البركات الأنماطي أنا ثابت بن بندار أنا عبيد الله بن أحمد بن عثمان الصيرفي أنا عبيد الله بن يعقوب أنا العباس بن العباس بن محمد الجوهري أنا صالح بن أحمد بن محمد بن حنبل نا أبي قال أسيد بن حضير أبو عتيك أنبأنا أبو الغنائم بن النرسي ثم حدثنا أبو الفضل بن ناصر نا أبو الفضل بن خيرون وأبو الحسين بن الطيوري وأبو الغنائم بن النرسي واللفظ له قالوا أنا أحمد الواسطي زاد ابن خيرون وأبو الحسين الأصبهاني قالا أنا أحمد بن عبدان أنا محمد بن إسماعيل.

Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 395), vol. 1, 639A, and vol. 2, P079A, vol. 2, 083A, vol. 2, 329A, vol. 2, 340A, vol. 2, 449A, vol. 2, 526A, vol. 2, 652A, vol. 2, 660A; and as a participant in the narative twice, vol. 2, 83A.

[^comment-ZTKXV01P080A-1]: Aymān b. ʿUbayd is mentioned in <a href="WZATB.html" class="witness-link">WZATB</a> (Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ṭufayl al-Kūfī al-Bakkāʾī al-ʿĀmirī) on <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV02P347C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 2 p. 347) following a poem about the Battle of Khaybar, in an account of the Battle of Ḥunayn on <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV02P442F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 2 p. 442) and p. 459B (at which he was killed). He is also mentioned in <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) in the story of Ḥunayn on <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV23P273A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 23 p. 273); <a href="WSFAB.html" class="witness-link">WSFAB</a> (Salamah b. al-Faḍl al-Abrash al-Azraqī al-Anṣārī al-Rāzī) on <a href="../references.html#ref-STBX" class="source-ref">STBXV01P288D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muʿjam al-kabīr</span>, vol. 1 p. 288), <a href="../references.html#ref-NYMX" class="source-ref">NYMXV01P318C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Nuʿaym</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Maʿrifat al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 1 p. 318), ibid., 318D, and <a href="../references.html#ref-TBRB" class="source-ref">TBRBV03P081B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk (1967)</span>, vol. 3 p. 81); and in an unwitnessed passage on <a href="../references.html#ref-NHXX" class="source-ref">NHXXV03P356C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd Allāh b. Yūsuf b. Muḥammad al-Zaylaʿī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Nasb al-rāyah li-aḥādīth al-hidāyah</span>, vol. 3 p. 356). He was Aymān b. ʿUbayd al-Ḥabashī, a <em>mawlā</em> of the prophet. He and Usāmah b. Zayd al-Ḥārithah share the same mother, who was Umm al-Ẓabāʾ <em>bint</em> Thaʿlabah b. ʿAmr (<a href="../references.html#ref-BRSX" class="source-ref">BRSXV01P128C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Istīʿāb fī maʿrifat al-aṣḥāb</span>, vol. 1 p. 128)). Placement will be in the biographical section.

[^comment-BKHBV02P351E-1]: Ḥumayd b. Yaʿqūb b. Yasār is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. <a href="../references.html#ref-ZTTH" class="source-ref">ZTTHV02P230A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Khaythamah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Tārīkh al-kabīr al-safar al-thālith</span>, vol. 2 p. 230) and <a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV03P231C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 3 p. 231) (below) state that Ḥumayd was a source for Ibn Isḥāq, although he does not appear elsewhere in the Ibn Isḥāq corpus. Saʿīd b. al-Musayb is mentioned in <a href="WZATB.html" class="witness-link">WZATB</a> (Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ṭufayl al-Kūfī al-Bakkāʾī al-ʿĀmirī), usually as a source for al-Zuhrī (<a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P400F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 400), vol. 2, 340C, 655C; also see <a href="../references.html#ref-TMMX" class="source-ref">TMMXV01P065B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Aḥmad al-Tamīmī al-Maghribī al-Ifrīrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Miḥan</span>, vol. 1 p. 65), 70B), ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Ḥarmalah al-Aslamī (<a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV02P414B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 2 p. 414)), or the “people of knowledge” (<a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P564C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 564)). His son, Muḥammad, is cited as a source for Ibn Isḥāq in a number of passages (<a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P169D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 169), vol. 1, 173D, 610E). Placement of the passage in the biography section.

[^comment-RZJXV03P231C-1]: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī states, &quot;حميد بن يعقوب بن يسار المدنى روى عن سعيد ابن المسيب روى عنه محمد بن إسحاق.&quot;

This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content. Passage refers to ṣadaqah. May belong in fiqh section or in post <em>hijrah</em> ritual section.
[^comment-HBHXV29P420A-1]: Acording to <a href="../references.html#ref-MDMX" class="source-ref">MDMXV01P265A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Mandah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Maʿrifat al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 1 p. 265) and <a href="../references.html#ref-BGHX" class="source-ref">BGHXV01P331A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Baghawī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Muʿjam al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 1 p. 331) is a variant of the tradition from Ibn Isḥāq via the copy of <a href="WSFAB.html" class="witness-link">WSFAB</a> (Salamah b. al-Faḍl al-Abrash al-Azraqī al-Anṣārī al-Rāzī), the &quot;man from the <em>Banī</em> al-Dayl&quot; is identified as Busr b. Miḥjān al-Duʿālī. It is not possible to place a day on the event described beyound that it happened in Madīnah. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.

[^comment-ZTTHV02P286A-1]: Dāwūd b. al-Ḥuṣayn al-Madinī, Abū Sulaymān, a <em>mawlā</em> of ʿAmr b. ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān. He heard from ʿIkramah, Abū Sufyān, a <em>mawlā</em> of Abū Aḥmad (<a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV03P231D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 3 p. 231) and <a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV03P408F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 3 p. 408)), ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj (<a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV03P408F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 3 p. 408)), and ʿUqbah b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (<a href="../references.html#ref-QNMX" class="source-ref">QNMXV02P157B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Qāniʿ</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Muʿjam al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 2 p. 157)). He also related to Mālik b. Anas, Ibn Isḥāq, Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar b. Abī Kathīr (<a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV03P231D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 3 p. 231)), Zayd b. Jubayr (<a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV03P390C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 3 p. 390)), ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar (<a href="../references.html#ref-WKKH" class="source-ref">WKKHV01P149A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Khalaf al-Wakīʿ</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Akhbār al-quḍāh</span>, vol. 1 p. 149)), Ibrāhīm b. Ismāʿīl b. Abī Ḥabībah al-Ashhalī (<a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV02P083F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 2 p. 83)), Yaḥyā b. al-ʿAlāʾ (<a href="../references.html#ref-QNMX" class="source-ref">QNMXV02P157B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Qāniʿ</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Muʿjam al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 2 p. 157)), and his son Sulaymān (<a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV04P111B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 4 p. 111)). He was generally considered trustworthy in the transmission of <em>ḥadīth</em> (<a href="../references.html#ref-JTTX" class="source-ref">JTTXV01P147B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿIjlī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-thiqāt</span>, vol. 1 p. 147) and <a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV03P409C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 3 p. 409)). He is sometimes listed as a <em>mawlā</em> of ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr b. ʿUthmān (<a href="../references.html#ref-ZTTH" class="source-ref">ZTTHV02P286A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Khaythamah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Tārīkh al-kabīr al-safar al-thālith</span>, vol. 2 p. 286)). He was also accused a being a member of the Khawārij, and he and ʿIkramah had to flee Madīnah due to these accusations. (ibid.). ʿIkramah was a <em>mawlā</em> of ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās (<a href="../references.html#ref-TBMD" class="source-ref">TBMDV01P008B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muntakhab min Kitāb dhayl al-mudhīl</span>, vol. 1 p. 8)). According to Ibn Ḥibbān, Dāwūd b. al-Ḥuṣayn died in Madīnah in the year 135/752 (<a href="../references.html#ref-BNTH" class="source-ref">BNTHV06P284A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥibbān</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Thiqāt</span>, vol. 6 p. 284)). Ibn Ḥibbān goes on to chastise readers for shunning Ibn Ḥuṣayn’s traditions because of his Kharajī sympathies (which he refers to as his <em>madhhab al-shurāh</em>), holding that “his traditions were not an introduction to his opinions.”

Placement is based on content. # @<a href="../references.html#ref-RJXX" class="source-ref">RJXXV03P242B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Maqdisī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Aḥādīth al-mukhtārah</span>, vol. 3 p. 242)_END_WSACD VAR_<a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV03P064A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 3 p. 64) VAR_<a href="../references.html#ref-KTHR" class="source-ref">KTHRV03P383B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Jāmiʿ al-masānīd waʾl-sunan</span>, vol. 3 p. 383) أخبرنا المبارك بن المعطوش الحربي أن هبة الله بن الحصين أخبرهم أنا أبو علي بن المذهب أنا أبو بكر القطيعي نا عبد الله بن أحمد حدثني أبي نا يعقوب نا أبي عن ابن إسحاق حدثني محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن الحصين أنه حدث عن سعد بن أبي وقاص أنه كان يصلي العشاء الآخرة في مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم يوتر بواحدة لا يزيد عليها قال فيقال له أتوتر بواحدة لا تزيد عليها يا أبا إسحاق فيقول نعم إني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول الذي لا ينام حتى يوتر حازم كذا رواه الإمام أحمد في مسنده وما أرى محمدا سمع من سعد والله أعلم. @<a href="../references.html#ref-RJXX" class="source-ref">RJXXV03P242B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Maqdisī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Aḥādīth al-mukhtārah</span>, vol. 3 p. 242)_BEG_WSACD 643 # @<a href="../references.html#ref-KTHR" class="source-ref">KTHRV03P383B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Jāmiʿ al-masānīd waʾl-sunan</span>, vol. 3 p. 383)_END_WSACD VAR_<a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV03P064A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 3 p. 64) VAR_<a href="../references.html#ref-RJXX" class="source-ref">RJXXV03P242B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Maqdisī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Aḥādīth al-mukhtārah</span>, vol. 3 p. 242) حدثنا يعقوب حدثنا أبى عن ابن إسحاق حدثنى محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن الحصين أنه حدث عن سعد بن أبى وقاص أنه كان يصلى العشاء الآخرة فى مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم يوتر بواحدة لا يزيد عليها قال فيقال له أتوتر بواحدة لا تزيد عليها يا أبا إسحاق فيقول نعم إنى سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول الذى لا ينام حتى يوتر حازم. @<a href="../references.html#ref-KTHR" class="source-ref">KTHRV03P383B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Jāmiʿ al-masānīd waʾl-sunan</span>, vol. 3 p. 383)_BEG_WSACD PageV03P383 774

Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 2 p. 276) states that ʿAbd Allāh b. Unays killed Kaʿb b. al-Ashrāf and includes a different poem of praise). For an quotation of a similar passage without a withness, see <a href="../references.html#ref-DHTI" class="source-ref">DHTIV03P207A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dhahabī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-Islām</span>, vol. 3 p. 207), <a href="../references.html#ref-MZTX" class="source-ref">MZTXV03P249A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 3 p. 249), <a href="../references.html#ref-MZTX" class="source-ref">MZTXV14P105A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 14 p. 105).

[^comment-HBRXV02P221A-1]: Salamah b. Dīnār is not metioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām but is metioned as a source for Ibn Isḥāq in the witness of <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī), although usually as Abū Ḥāzim. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV05P421B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 5 p. 421) to <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV05P422A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 5 p. 422) he died in 140.
[^comment-ZTKXV01P168A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.
[^comment-HBHXV37P490A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. <a href="../references.html#ref-KHGH" class="source-ref">KHGHV01P225A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khattābī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Gharīb al-ḥadīth</span>, vol. 1 p. 225) refers to this as the (قصة الملاعنة) &quot;qiṣṣah al-malāʿanah&quot; (the story of the calling down of the curse). In the well known story that refers to the revelation of Qurʾān 24:1-10 and the first instance of liʿān, a woman (sometimes identified as Khawlah <em>bint</em> Qays b. Muḥasin [<a href="../references.html#ref-HMMX" class="source-ref">HMMXV03P386A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Al-Ḥusayn b. Masʿūd b. Muḥammad al-Baghawī al-Shāfiʿī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Maʿālim al-tanzīl fī tafsīr al-Qurʾān</span>, vol. 3 p. 386)]), who had become pregnant, was accused of having ilicit sex, which she denied. Lacking four witnesses to the actual act, she vowed she was not guilty, and called curses down on herself if she was. The woman was married to the cousin of ʿĀsim b. ʿAdī (identified variously as Ḥilāl b. Umayyah [<a href="../references.html#ref-ANSS" class="source-ref">ANSSV06P172A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Nasāʾī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sunan al-ṣughrā</span>, vol. 6 p. 172)] or ʿUwaymir al-Anṣārī [<a href="../references.html#ref-MSTM" class="source-ref">MSTMV05P145A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sakāwī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Al-Tuḥfat al-laṭifat fī taʾrīkh al-Madīnat al-Sharīfat</span>, vol. 5 p. 145)], ʿUwaymir b. Ubayd (أبيض) al-Anṣārī al-ʿAjlānī, or ʿUwaymir b. al-Ḥārith b. Zayd b. Ḥārithah b. al-Jadd b. al-ʿAjlān [<a href="../references.html#ref-NWXX" class="source-ref">NWXXV02P041A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Nawawī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-asmāʾ waʾl-lughāt</span>, vol. 2 p. 41)] all of whom were members of the Banu al-ʿAjlān b. ʿAmr b. ʿAwf) and Muhammad advised ʿĀsim that the proof of the accusation would be the child&#x27;s physical appearance (see <a href="../references.html#ref-MSTM" class="source-ref">MSTMV03P184A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sakāwī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Al-Tuḥfat al-laṭifat fī taʾrīkh al-Madīnat al-Sharīfat</span>, vol. 3 p. 184) to <a href="../references.html#ref-MSTM" class="source-ref">MSTMV03P187A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sakāwī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Al-Tuḥfat al-laṭifat fī taʾrīkh al-Madīnat al-Sharīfat</span>, vol. 3 p. 187) for an early detailed account). <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV37P490A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 37 p. 490) identifies the accused man as Ibn al-Saḥmāʾ, whom <a href="../references.html#ref-MSTM" class="source-ref">MSTMV03P184A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sakāwī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Al-Tuḥfat al-laṭifat fī taʾrīkh al-Madīnat al-Sharīfat</span>, vol. 3 p. 184) identifies as Sharīk b. al-Saḥmāʾ. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-JWTX" class="source-ref">JWTXV01P509A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Jawzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Talqīḥ fuhūm ahl al-athar fī ʿuyūn al-Tārīkh waʾl-siyar</span>, vol. 1 p. 509), al-Saḥmāʾ was Sharīk&#x27;s mother, who was otherwise known as Umm al-Barrāʾ b. Mālik. Sharīk&#x27;s father was ʿAbdah b. Muʿaṭṭib (<a href="../references.html#ref-JWTX" class="source-ref">JWTXV01P509A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Jawzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Talqīḥ fuhūm ahl al-athar fī ʿuyūn al-Tārīkh waʾl-siyar</span>, vol. 1 p. 509)) or ʿAbdah b. Mughīth b. al-Jadd b. al-ʿAjlān (<a href="../references.html#ref-BRSX" class="source-ref">BRSXV02P821A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Istīʿāb fī maʿrifat al-aṣḥāb</span>, vol. 2 p. 821)). ʿAbdah b. Muʿaṭṭib, Sharīk, Umm al-Barrāʾ, and al-Barrāʾ b. Mālik are not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. for a version via the witness of <a href="WYUAU.html" class="witness-link">WYUAU</a> (Yaʿlā b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Umayyah al-Īyādī al-Tanāfisī al-Kūfī), see <a href="../references.html#ref-KHGH" class="source-ref">KHGHV01P225A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khattābī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Gharīb al-ḥadīth</span>, vol. 1 p. 225).
[^comment-QSDXV03P1198A-1]: ʿĀsim b. ʿUmar b. Qatādah is a common source for Ibn Isḥāq . He is mentioned frequently in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. The context for this passage is obscur. It is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām nor are there any other references to it via other transmitters. It appears to be a clarification on the identity of a particular type of food and it is not clear how this fits in the overall compisition of the text.

He transmitted diectly to Ibn Isḥāq and is not an eye witness. Passage may not belong to the Maghāzī copied by Ibn Saʿd and inclusion is provisional.
[^comment-JJKXV07P264B-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV04P225A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 4 p. 225) to <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV04P226A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 4 p. 226) states ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Awfī was a companion who participated in seven campaigns with the prophet. He was also known as Ibn Abī Awfī. He traveled to Kūfah where he died in 86. He is said to have been present at Ḥudaybīyah (<a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV06P98A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 6 p. 98)). <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV06P98A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 6 p. 98) and <a href="../references.html#ref-MDFX" class="source-ref">MDFXV01P101A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Mandah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Fatḥ al-bāb fī al-kunā waʾl-alqāb</span>, vol. 1 p. 101) identifies Abū Awfā as ʿAlqamah b. Khālid b. al-Ḥārith b. Abī Usayd b. Rifāʿah b. Thaʿlabah b. Hawāzin b. Aslam b. Aqṣā b. Ḥārithah b. ʿAmr b. ʿĀmir al-Aslamī. ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Awfī is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. A Nuʿmān b. Abī Awfā is mentioned as one of Muḥammad&#x27;s Jewish adversaries among the <em>Banū</em> Qaynuqāʿ, see <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P514A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 514). ʿAlqamah b. Khālid is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām.

[^comment-RZJXV05P271C-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. This is an attribution fragment for ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAmmār b. Abī Zaynab. His full name was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAmmār b. Abī Zaynab al-Taymī al-Madinī. He is recorded as transmitting from just two people: al-Qāsim b. Muḥammad b. Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq and Abū Bakr b. Muḥammad b. ʿAmr b. Ḥazm. Besides Ibn Isḥāq, he also related stories to Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān and Yazīd b. ʿAbd al-Allāh b. al-Hād (<a href="../references.html#ref-MZTX" class="source-ref">MZTXV17P295B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 17 p. 295)). No date of death is found. He is not mentioned as a source or a character in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. There does not appear to be any extant traditions that Ibn Isḥāq related from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAmmār and he is not otherwise mentioned in the corpus. Placement in the <em>Ṭabaqāt</em> section.

The source for the entry is Saʿīd b. Abī Hind al-Fazārī, a mawlā of Samarah b. Jandab, who is mentioned twice in <a href="WZATB.html" class="witness-link">WZATB</a> (Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ṭufayl al-Kūfī al-Bakkāʾī al-ʿĀmirī) (<a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV02P411C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 2 p. 411) and vol. 2, 541D). ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī, the subject of the passage, is not mentioned as a character or as a source in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV06P152D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 6 p. 152) to p. 154E, he was ʿUbaydah b. Qays al-Salmāni. Ibn Saʿd states that he submitted two years before the death of the prophet and that he related from ʿUmar, ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, and ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd. He was one of the principal leaders of the <em>banū</em> Murād in Kūfah and is said to have kept notes of the traditions he collected but destroyed them late in life for fear that they might be misused or corrupted after his death. He also appears to have practiced asceticism, as was common among <em>ḥadīth</em> enthusiasts. ʿUbaydah died in the year 72/691-2. <a href="../references.html#ref-JTTX" class="source-ref">JTTXV01P325B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿIjlī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-thiqāt</span>, vol. 1 p. 325) considers him a successor (<em>tābiʿī</em>) not a companion, even though he submitted two years before the death of the prophet, because he never saw the prophet. <a href="../references.html#ref-WKKH" class="source-ref">WKKHV02P399A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Khalaf al-Wakīʿ</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Akhbār al-quḍāh</span>, vol. 2 p. 399) lists a number of quotations from ʿUbaydah on ʿAlī’s advice on adjudication. Ibn Abī Ḥātim gives his name as ʿUbaydah b. ʿAmr al-Salmānī and states that Yaḥyā b. Maʿīn considered him trustworthy (<a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV06P091C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 6 p. 91)). Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī states that there was no agreement on his name and gives several variations, in addition to the above, ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī al-Murādī al-Hamdānī, ʿUbaydah b. Qays b. ʿAmr, Abū Muslim, and Abū ʿAmr. He also states that ʿUbaydah fought that the Battle of Nahrawān with ʿAlī against the Khawārijī revolt. (<a href="../references.html#ref-KHTG" class="source-ref">KHTGV12P422A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</span>, vol. 12 p. 422)). <a href="../references.html#ref-KBSS" class="source-ref">KBSSV10P023B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAlī b. Khalaf b. Baṭṭāl</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī</span>, vol. 10 p. 23) quotes Ibn Isḥāq in an unwitnessed account that ʿUbaydah was at the Battle of Ṣiffīn with ʿAlī (this statement is not found elsewhere in the corpus). In addition to Saʿīd b. Abī Hind al-Fazārī, he related to Muslim b. Nisṭān (<a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV07P274C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 7 p. 274)), Muḥammad b. Sīrīn (<a href="../references.html#ref-JTTX" class="source-ref">JTTXV01P325B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿIjlī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-thiqāt</span>, vol. 1 p. 325)), Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī (ibid.), ʿĀmir b. Sharāḥīl b. ʿAbd al-Shaʿbī (who is normally listed simply as “al-Shaʿbī”—<a href="../references.html#ref-ZTTH" class="source-ref">ZTTHV03P142B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Khaythamah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Tārīkh al-kabīr al-safar al-thālith</span>, vol. 3 p. 142)), Muḥammad b. Sulaymān (<a href="../references.html#ref-WKKH" class="source-ref">WKKHV02P399A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Khalaf al-Wakīʿ</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Akhbār al-quḍāh</span>, vol. 2 p. 399)), al-Nuʿmān b. Qays al-Murādī al-Kūfī (<a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV08P446E</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 8 p. 446)), Muslim b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Ajrad (<a href="../references.html#ref-MRSX" class="source-ref">MRSXV02P236C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Bakr Aḥmad b. ʿAlī b. Manjuwayh</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Rijāl Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim</span>, vol. 2 p. 236)), Abū Ḥuṣayn (<a href="../references.html#ref-KHTG" class="source-ref">KHTGV12P422A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</span>, vol. 12 p. 422)), ʿAmr b. Murrah (<a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV33P091B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 33 p. 91)), and ʿAbd Allāh b. Salamah al-Hamdānī (ibid.).

Salamah b. Dīnār al-Baṣrī) on <a href="../references.html#ref-ADTM" class="source-ref">ADTMV03P661A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Dāwūd Sulaymān b. Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad Abī Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī</span>, vol. 3 p. 661) and <a href="../references.html#ref-ZTTH" class="source-ref">ZTTHV01P215A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Khaythamah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Tārīkh al-kabīr al-safar al-thālith</span>, vol. 1 p. 215).
[^comment-ZTTHV03P063A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. It is drawn from Ibn Abī Khaythamah’s biography of al-Aswad b. Yazīd, the father of Ibn Isḥāq’s source, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Aswad. The passage is meant to establish the relationship between al-Aswad b. Yazīd, his uncle ʿAlqamah b. Qays b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Nakhaʿī, and ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb. Since ʿAlqamah was closely associated with ʿAlī, and fought on his side at Ṣiffīn, it is also designed to show that he and al-Aswad were a part of the mainstream. No date is given for the scene and the passage will be placed in the biographical section for both ʿal-Aswad and ʿAlqamah.
[^comment-ZTTHV03P098A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. It is drawn from Ibn Abī Khaythamah’s biography of ʿAlqamah b. Qays, the uncle of Ibn Isḥāq’s source, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Aswad. This appears to be the only instance of this fragment in the Ibn Isḥāq corpus.
[^comment-HBHXV02P111A-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV02P111A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 2 p. 111) places this passage in the chapter referring the traditions of ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib.

[^comment-HBHXV01P424A-1]: According to <a href="../references.html#ref-BQSX" class="source-ref">BQSXV06P360A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 6 p. 360), this event appears to have occured during the Caliphate of ʿUmar and deals with the payment of blood money. There is also an illusion to the story of Muḥammad&#x27;s flight from Mecca found in <a href="WZATB.html" class="witness-link">WZATB</a> (Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ṭufayl al-Kūfī al-Bakkāʾī al-ʿĀmirī) on <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P489A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 489) as both quotations involve Surāqah b. Mālik b. Juʿshum. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.
[^comment-BKHBV01P327A-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV01P327A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 1 p. 327) is placed in the biography of the transmitter of the passage, Ibrāhīm b. Mūsā b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. No other context is given. Ibrāhīm b. Mūsā is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Rabīʿah b. al-Mughīrah al-Makhzūmī is mentioned by Ibn Isḥāq in the redaction of Ibn Hishām as being one of the two Qurashīs sent to Abyssinia for retrieve migrants (<a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P333A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 333) to vol. 1, 337A, and also in the witness of <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) see <a href="../references.html#ref-HBFX" class="source-ref">HBFXV01P278A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Faḍāʾil al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 1 p. 278), <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV03P263A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 3 p. 263), <a href="../references.html#ref-NYHX" class="source-ref">NYHXV01P115A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Nuʿaym</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ḥilyat al-awlīyāʾ wa-ṭabaqāt al-aṣfīyāʾ</span>, vol. 1 p. 115), and <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV37P170A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 37 p. 170)). He is also described as being one of the instigators of the Battle of Uḥud (<a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV02P060A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 2 p. 60), for the witness of bn Saʿd see <a href="../references.html#ref-DHRQ" class="source-ref">DHRQV01P353A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Mundhir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb tafsīr al-Qurʾān</span>, vol. 1 p. 353)). ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Rabīʿah is cited as a witness to ʿUmar in several traditions (see <a href="../references.html#ref-MDRX" class="source-ref">MDRXV04P2044A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Dārimī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad al-Dārimī</span>, vol. 4 p. 2044), <a href="../references.html#ref-KTMX" class="source-ref">KTMXV03P855A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿUmar b. Shabbah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb taʾrīkh al-Madīnah al-munawwarah</span>, vol. 3 p. 855), <a href="../references.html#ref-DKHX" class="source-ref">DKHXV05P474A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. ʿAmr b. Abī ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Āḥād waʾl-mathānī</span>, vol. 5 p. 474) in a passage from Ibn Isḥāq witnessed by <a href="WYSAU.html" class="witness-link">WYSAU</a> (Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd b. Abān al-Qurashī al-Umawī al-Kūfī)). He was appointed govenor of Yemen by ʿUmar and remaioned in that position after the rise of ʿUthmān, for whom he advocated during the majlis following ʿUmar&#x27;s murder (<a href="../references.html#ref-TBRC" class="source-ref">TBRCV01P2785A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk</span>, vol. 1 p. 2785)). According to <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV05P009A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 5 p. 9) he died during the siege of ʿUthmān&#x27;s home when, in the rush to assist him, ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Rabīʿah fell from his camel and died. Note: <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV01P327A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 1 p. 327) might belong in the attributes of ʿUmar section, that often follows an important person&#x27;s death. Will leave in biography section unless more evidence arrises that supports placement elsewhere. <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV01P327A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 1 p. 327) refers to the moring prayer at al-Muzdalifah on the morning of the third day of the pilgrimage. According to Ibn Isḥāq, ʿUmar led the pilgrimage for the first time in 12/634 (see <a href="../references.html#ref-TBRC" class="source-ref">TBRCV01P2078A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk</span>, vol. 1 p. 2078)). Quoting Ibn ʿUmar, al-Ṭabarī also states that ʿUmar led the pilgrimage every year of his caliphate except to the first (<a href="../references.html#ref-TBRC" class="source-ref">TBRCV01P2212B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk</span>, vol. 1 p. 2212)). <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV01P296A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 1 p. 296) quotes Ibn Isḥāq as transmitting another tradition from Ibrāhīm b. Mūsā b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān but does not provide a witness. Ibn Isḥāq is quoted as saying: وقد روى ابن إسحاق سمع ابراهيم بن موسى ابن عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن أبي ربيعة عن عكرمة بن خالد ومات عبد الله بن أبي ربيعة قبل عثمان بقليل وكانت أم كلثوم تحت طلحة فكأن عبد الرحمن تزوجها. It appears, therefore that Ibrāhīm b. Mūsā was a source of biographical material. Based on Shamela search (9/15/22) these are the only references to any tradition related by Ibrāhīm b. Mūsā to Ibn Isḥāq. This appears to be the only reference to the passage in the corpus. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-MISM" class="source-ref">MISMV01P377A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Idrīs al-Shāfiʿī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Musnad</span>, vol. 1 p. 377), ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Rabīʿah had married a woman whom ʿUmar later married. ʿUmar divorced her before consummating the marriage.
