[^comment-BKHBV06P532A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām nor is ʿUmayr. al-Dhahabī states that ʿUmayr was the <em>mawlā</em> of Umm al-Faḍl <em>bint</em> al-Ḥārith, although others asserted that he was the <em>mawlā</em> of ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās. He was supposed to have only related stories from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās, Usāmah b. Zayd, Abū Juhaym, and Umm al-Faḍl <em>bint</em> al-Ḥārith (<a href="../references.html#ref-DHTI" class="source-ref">DHTIV07P209A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dhahabī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-Islām</span>, vol. 7 p. 209)). Ibn Manjuwayh states that he was the <em>mawlā</em> of Umm al-Faḍl <em>bint</em> al-Ḥārith and that he died in Madīnah in 104/722 (<a href="../references.html#ref-MRSX" class="source-ref">MRSXV02P088D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Bakr Aḥmad b. ʿAlī b. Manjuwayh</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Rijāl Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim</span>, vol. 2 p. 88)). This is a standard identity clarification usually inserted following the first entry for a person or after some important event involving that person. Placement is based on the above collection of traditions is the only reference to ʿUmayr in the corpus.
[^comment-ZTTHV02P278A-1]: Iyāḍ b. Dīnār al-Laythī is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. He is mentioned in <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) as a source in a single passage about the ḥajj of the year 64. ʿĪyāḍ b. Dīnār is also listed as a source in another story in <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) on <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRT" class="source-ref">HJRTV14P481B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Itḥāf al-maharah bi-al-fawāʾid al-mubtakarah min aṭrāf al-ʿasharah</span>, vol. 14 p. 481) and <a href="../references.html#ref-HJII" class="source-ref">HJIIV07P168D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Iṭrāf al-musnid al-maʿtalī bi-Iṭrāf al-musnad al-Ḥanbalī</span>, vol. 7 p. 168). He appears in only a few traditions overall in the Ibn Isḥāq corpus. He is primarily cited as a source for Ibn Isḥāq (see <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV07P022E</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 7 p. 22), <a href="../references.html#ref-BNTH" class="source-ref">BNTHV05P267B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥibbān</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Thiqāt</span>, vol. 5 p. 267) [that states he also related from Abū Hurayrah], <a href="../references.html#ref-THMX" class="source-ref">THMXV01P180G</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Shāhīn</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tārīkh asmāʾ al-thiqāt</span>, vol. 1 p. 180), and <a href="../references.html#ref-MAHH" class="source-ref">MAHHV01P328A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. Ḥamzah al-Ḥusaynī al-Dimashqī al-Shāfiʿī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Ikmāl fī dhikr man lahu riwāyah fī Musnad al-Imām Aḥmad min al-rijāl siwā man dhukira fī Tahdhīb al-kamāl</span>, vol. 1 p. 328)). According to <a href="../references.html#ref-MSTM" class="source-ref">MSTMV02P364G</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sakāwī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Al-Tuḥfat al-laṭifat fī taʾrīkh al-Madīnat al-Sharīfat</span>, vol. 2 p. 364), he was one of the &quot;People of Madīnah&quot; among the fourth generation of successors. He is only cited as transmitting from Abū Hurayrah and to Ibn Isḥāq. no date of death is mentioned. In addition to <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī), Ibn Isḥāq related traditions from ʿĪyāḍ b. Dīnār via <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī) (<a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV35P142B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 35 p. 142), <a href="../references.html#ref-NZDX" class="source-ref">NZDXV14P312D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Manẓūr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Mukhtaṣar Taʾrīkh Dimashq</span>, vol. 14 p. 312), and <a href="../references.html#ref-DHSN" class="source-ref">DHSNV13P312E</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dhahabī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Siyar aʿlām al-nubalāʾ</span>, vol. 13 p. 312); and <a href="WHAYA.html" class="witness-link">WHAYA</a> (Yazīd b. Hārūn al-Wāsiṭī) on <a href="../references.html#ref-AYFN" class="source-ref">AYFNV01P140A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Ṣawāf</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Fawāʾid Abū Bakr al-Naṣībī</span>, vol. 1 p. 140), <a href="../references.html#ref-NYSJ" class="source-ref">NYSJV02P091A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Nuʿaym</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṣifah al-jannah</span>, vol. 2 p. 91), <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRT" class="source-ref">HJRTV14P481B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Itḥāf al-maharah bi-al-fawāʾid al-mubtakarah min aṭrāf al-ʿasharah</span>, vol. 14 p. 481), and <a href="../references.html#ref-HJII" class="source-ref">HJIIV07P168D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Iṭrāf al-musnid al-maʿtalī bi-Iṭrāf al-musnad al-Ḥanbalī</span>, vol. 7 p. 168). He is also a source for a passage in <a href="WSFAB.html" class="witness-link">WSFAB</a> (Salamah b. al-Faḍl al-Abrash al-Azraqī al-Anṣārī al-Rāzī) dealing with the commentary of Qurʾān 2:213 (see @<a href="../references.html#ref-TBJB" class="source-ref">TBJBV04P283C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Jāmiʿ al-bayān ʿan tāʾwīl āy al-Qurʾān</span>, vol. 4 p. 283)).
[^comment-ZTKXV01P500C-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-ZTKX" class="source-ref">ZTKXV01P500C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Khaythamah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Tārīkh al-kabīr sifr al-thānī</span>, vol. 1 p. 500) quotes Ibn Isḥāq to highlight a dispute over the indenty of Faḍālah. Some assert he is Faḍālah b. ʿUbayd b. Nāfidh but Ibn Isḥāq is quoted as stating, via <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī), that he is Faḍālah &quot;from&quot; (<em>min</em>) the ʿUbayd b. Nāfidh clan. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-DRQM" class="source-ref">DRQMV02P694A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dāraquṭnī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muʾtalif waʾl-mukhtalif</span>, vol. 2 p. 694), in a non-Ibn Isḥāq tradition, Hanash al-Sanʿānī is quoted as saying that he and Faḍālah participated together in a battle in which he and his companions were awarded a necklace (كنا مع فضالة بن عبيد في غزوة فطارت لي ولأصحابي قلادة) in a statement analogous to <a href="../references.html#ref-MDMX" class="source-ref">MDMXV01P645A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Mandah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Maʿrifat al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 1 p. 645) found above in the story of the Battle of Khaybar. This scene is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. <a href="../references.html#ref-BRSX" class="source-ref">BRSXV03P1262D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Istīʿāb fī maʿrifat al-aṣḥāb</span>, vol. 3 p. 1262) identifies another person by the name of Faḍālah b. ʿUbayd b. Nāqid b. Qays b. Ṣuhayb al-Anṣārī a;-Awsī al-ʿUmarī, Abū Muḥammad. He first participated at Uḥud and then all subsequent battles, eventually participating in the conquest of Syria before settling in Damascus. He was appointed judge of the city under Muʿāwiyah and participated as a judge at Ṣifīn. His date of death of placed variously as 53, 55, or 67 with the most likely being toward the end of the caliphate of Muʿāwiyah, during the invasion of Rhodes in 55/674-75 (see <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHB" class="source-ref">KTHBV08P078B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bidāyat waʾl-nihāyah</span>, vol. 8 p. 78)). <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV48P290B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 48 p. 290) identifies the same person, but with the name Faḍālah b. ʿUbayd b. Nāfid b. Qays b. Ṣuhayb. The similarity of the names &quot;Nāfidh&quot; (نافذ), &quot;Nāqid&quot; (ناقد), and &quot;Nāfid&quot; (نافد) means that a simple slip of the pen might change the name of the individual and it was not uncommon to have disputes over naming such as this.
[^comment-ZTTHV02P329A-1]: This passage is not located in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. This is an identity passage, here to establish that Ibn Isḥāq had met al-Qāsim b. Muḥammad. al-Qāsim b. Muḥammad b. Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq was the grandson of the first caliph. His daughter, Farwah, was married to Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. Ḥusayn, b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib. He was known as a critic of the Qadarīyah movement and a collector of traditions, which he arranged alphabetically. He died in 108, at the age of 70 or 72 (<a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV05P142C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 5 p. 142) to <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV05P148F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 5 p. 148)). Ibn Isḥāq is quoted in unwitnessed passages speaking about the qualities of al-Qāsim b. Muḥammad, giving the impression that he knew him fairly well (<a href="../references.html#ref-JWSS" class="source-ref">JWSSV01P351I</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ibn Jawzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṣifat al-ṣafwah</span>, vol. 1 p. 351), as well as <a href="../references.html#ref-JWZX" class="source-ref">JWZXV07P123C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Jawzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muntaẓam fī Tārīkh al-mulūk waʾl-umam</span>, vol. 7 p. 123)), similar fragments are also found in <a href="WYBWS.html" class="witness-link">WYBWS</a> (Yūnus b. Bukayr b. Wāṣil al-Shaybānī al-Jamāl al-Kūfī), <a href="WAZID.html" class="witness-link">WAZID</a> (ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. Muḥammad b. ʿUbayd b. Abī ʿUbayd al-Darāwardī), and <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī). He is mentioned as a link in six different chains of transmission in HSNX, but in none of these is he mentioned as a direct source. Ibn Isḥāq does transmit directly from his son, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Qāsim b. Muḥammad, in <a href="WZATB.html" class="witness-link">WZATB</a> (Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ṭufayl al-Kūfī al-Bakkāʾī al-ʿĀmirī) on <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV02P381B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 2 p. 381) (also see <a href="WSHAK.html" class="witness-link">WSHAK</a> (Sulaymān b. Ḥayyān al-Azdī al-Aḥmar al-Kūfī al-Jaʿfarī)). al-Qāsim b. Muḥammad is also mentioned in <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) in several places. In addition, he is cited in traditions related via <a href="WISUL.html" class="witness-link">WISUL</a> (Ismāʿīl b. ʿUlayah), <a href="WMHAL.html" class="witness-link">WMHAL</a> (Muḥammad b. al-Ḥajjāj al-Lakhmī), <a href="WYBWS.html" class="witness-link">WYBWS</a> (Yūnus b. Bukayr b. Wāṣil al-Shaybānī al-Jamāl al-Kūfī), and <a href="WSFAB.html" class="witness-link">WSFAB</a> (Salamah b. al-Faḍl al-Abrash al-Azraqī al-Anṣārī al-Rāzī). <a href="WMSAH.html" class="witness-link">WMSAH</a> (Muḥammad b. Salamah b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Bāhilī al-Ḥarrānī) includes a story in which al-Qāsim b. Muḥammad is a character as well as traditions in which he is a transmitter.
[^comment-HBHXV24P322A-1]: This passage refers to the well known incident usually referred to as the &quot;stoning of Māʿzin b. Mālik.&quot; This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām.
[^comment-BKTMV01P340A-1]: Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar b. Zubayr is cited in the redaction of Ibn Hishām 24 times as a transmitter to Ibn Isḥāq. Passage may not have been part of the Maghāzī copied by Ibn Saʿd. This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.
[^comment-BKHBV01P054B-1]: This passage is drawn from the biography for Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar b. Zubayr.
[^comment-ZTTHV02P277A-1]: Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Aswad b. Nawfal (or Nawfal b. al-Aswad) in not mention in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. He is, however, mentioned over 42 times in <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) (as of this writing). According to <a href="WZATB.html" class="witness-link">WZATB</a> (Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ṭufayl al-Kūfī al-Bakkāʾī al-ʿĀmirī) (<a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P324F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 324)), his grandfather, al-Aswad b. Nawfal b. Khuwaylid b. Asad b. Quṣayy was on of those to emigrated to Abyssinia. al-Aswad b. Nawfal was also the maternal cousin of Khadījah, the prophet’s wife (<a href="../references.html#ref-THRX" class="source-ref">THRXV01P233A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Athīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Usd al-ghābah fī maʿrifat al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 1 p. 233)). <a href="../references.html#ref-MZTX" class="source-ref">MZTXV25P646A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 25 p. 646) and other sources refer to him as “ʿUrwah’s orphan” (يتيم عروة) meaning that ʿUrwah adopted him. Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān went to Egypt in 136, according to ʿAbd Allāh b. Lahīʿah (?), and died there. He was bequeathed to ʿUrwah when his father died and that is why he is called “yatayam ʿUrwah.”
[^comment-ZTTHV02P228A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.
[^comment-MYWXV13P408A-1]: This passage seems to be evaluative. Similar evaluative traditions are found in the biographies of Maʿbad b. Kaʿb (see <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV37P291A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 37 p. 291))and Abū Hurayrah (see <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV15P78A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 15 p. 78)). This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.
[^comment-JHASV01P087A-1]: Musṭaḥ b. Uthānah was one of the emigrants to Madīnah. His mentioned on <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P478A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 478) (where he stayed when he arrived in Madīnah), vol. 1, 678A (mentioned as present at Badr and is most similar to the first part of the quotation in <a href="../references.html#ref-JHAS" class="source-ref">JHASV01P087A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Jayyānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Alqāb al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 1 p. 87)), vol. 2, 299A to 307A (where he is described as one of the men who accused ʿĀʾishah of adultry and corresponds with the second half of the passage on <a href="../references.html#ref-JHAS" class="source-ref">JHASV01P087A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Jayyānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Alqāb al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 1 p. 87)), and vol. 2, 351A (when he is mentioned as receiving a portion of the spoils of Khaybar). al-Ifk refers to the slander of those who accused ʿĀʾishah of adultry. In <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV02P297A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 2 p. 297) the group of accusers is referred to as the &quot;Ahl al-Ifk.&quot; For references to the story of the accusations against ʿĀʾishah via the witness of <a href="WJHZA.html" class="witness-link">WJHZA</a> (Jarīr b. Ḥāzim b. Zayd b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Shajāʿ al-Azdī al-ʿAtkī al-Baṣrī), see <a href="../references.html#ref-SFTX" class="source-ref">SFTXV01P080A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ al-Shaybānī al-ʿAṣfarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh</span>, vol. 1 p. 80); via the witness of <a href="WBSAB.html" class="witness-link">WBSAB</a> (Bakr b. Sulaymān al-Aswārī al-Baṣrī) see, <a href="../references.html#ref-SFTX" class="source-ref">SFTXV01P080A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ al-Shaybānī al-ʿAṣfarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh</span>, vol. 1 p. 80); via the witness of <a href="WSFAB.html" class="witness-link">WSFAB</a> (Salamah b. al-Faḍl al-Abrash al-Azraqī al-Anṣārī al-Rāzī), see <a href="../references.html#ref-TBRC" class="source-ref">TBRCV02P610A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk</span>, vol. 2 p. 610) to <a href="../references.html#ref-TBRC" class="source-ref">TBRCV02P619A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk</span>, vol. 2 p. 619); via the witness of <a href="WYBWS.html" class="witness-link">WYBWS</a> (Yūnus b. Bukayr b. Wāṣil al-Shaybānī al-Jamāl al-Kūfī), see <a href="../references.html#ref-BQWX" class="source-ref">BQWXV04P074A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Dalāʾil al-nubūwah wa maʿarifah aḥwāl ṣāḥib al-sharīʿah</span>, vol. 4 p. 74), <a href="../references.html#ref-DHTI" class="source-ref">DHTIV02P279A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dhahabī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-Islām</span>, vol. 2 p. 279); without a witness, see <a href="../references.html#ref-MQCX" class="source-ref">MQCXV05P016A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Muṭahhar b. Ṭāhir al-Maqdisī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Badʾ waʾl-taʾrīkh</span>, vol. 5 p. 16), <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHS" class="source-ref">KTHSV03P303A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrat al-nubuwīyah</span>, vol. 3 p. 303), <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHS" class="source-ref">KTHSV03P304A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrat al-nubuwīyah</span>, vol. 3 p. 304), <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHS" class="source-ref">KTHSV03P311A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrat al-nubuwīyah</span>, vol. 3 p. 311) <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHF" class="source-ref">KTHFV01P183A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Fuṣūl fī al-sīrah</span>, vol. 1 p. 183), <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHB" class="source-ref">KTHBV04P156A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bidāyat waʾl-nihāyah</span>, vol. 4 p. 156) to <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHB" class="source-ref">KTHBV04P164A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bidāyat waʾl-nihāyah</span>, vol. 4 p. 164), <a href="../references.html#ref-QZHX" class="source-ref">QZHXV01P220A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Maqrīzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Imtāʿ al-asmāʿ bi-mā li-l-nabī min al-aḥwāl waʾl-amwāl waʾl-hafadat waʾl-mutāʿ</span>, vol. 1 p. 220), <a href="../references.html#ref-QZHX" class="source-ref">QZHXV08P369A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Maqrīzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Imtāʿ al-asmāʿ bi-mā li-l-nabī min al-aḥwāl waʾl-amwāl waʾl-hafadat waʾl-mutāʿ</span>, vol. 8 p. 369).
[^comment-ZTKXV01P543A-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement is based on content.
[^comment-HBHXV37P291A-1]: This passage seems to be evaluative. Similar evaluative traditiona are found in the biographies of Muḥammad b. Muslim b. [^comment-TKXXV03P375A-1]: See <a href="../references.html#ref-BRSX" class="source-ref">BRSXV04P1503A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Istīʿāb fī maʿrifat al-aṣḥāb</span>, vol. 4 p. 1503), <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV62P143A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 62 p. 143), and <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRS" class="source-ref">HJRSV06P366A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Iṣābah fī tamyīz al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 6 p. 366) for a quotation of <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV03P375A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 3 p. 375) without a witness. For a reference to Nuʿmān&#x27;s presence at Badr, see via the witness of <a href="WYSAU.html" class="witness-link">WYSAU</a> (Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd b. Abān al-Qurashī al-Umawī al-Kūfī) in <a href="../references.html#ref-SHMS" class="source-ref">SHMSV04P120A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Yūsuf al-Ṣāliḥī al-Shāmī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Subul al-hudā waʾl-rashād fī Sīrat Khayr al-ʿibād</span>, vol. 4 p. 120).
[^comment-HBHXV32P210A-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-HHMX" class="source-ref">HHMXV07P379A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Razzāq b. Hammām al-Ḥumayrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muṣannaf</span>, vol. 7 p. 379) places this in the context of Ibn al-Nuʿmān and <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV03P375A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 3 p. 375) quotes a portion of the passage in the biography of al-Nuʿmān b. ʿAmr (although he appears to suggest that Ibn Isḥāq names him as al-Nuʿaymān). <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV03P375A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 3 p. 375) states that Nuʿaymān b. ʿAmr was the younger brother of Nuʿmān b. ʿAmr. Ibn al-Nuʿaymān or al-Nuʿaymān is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. He is sometimes identified as al-Nuʿaymān b. ʿAmr b. Rifāʿah b. al-Ḥārith. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-JWZX" class="source-ref">JWZXV05P277A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Jawzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muntaẓam fī Tārīkh al-mulūk waʾl-umam</span>, vol. 5 p. 277), al-Nuʿaymān participated in Badr, and all of the famous battles in which Muḥammad fought. He was known to have repeatedly been punished for drinking nabīdh. <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV06P431A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 6 p. 431) and <a href="../references.html#ref-TBRC" class="source-ref">TBRCV11P554A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk</span>, vol. 11 p. 554) mention the account of ʿUqbah b. al-Ḥārith where he describes being ordered by Muḥammad to beat Ibn Nuʿaymān or al-Nuʿaymān with shoes and palm branches for drinking. <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV03P375A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 3 p. 375) states he died in during the caliphate of Muʿawīyah but <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHB" class="source-ref">KTHBV08P070A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bidāyat waʾl-nihāyah</span>, vol. 8 p. 70) places his death in the year 54. <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRS" class="source-ref">HJRSV06P353A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Iṣābah fī tamyīz al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 6 p. 353) states that Ibn Isḥāq identifies him as al-Nuʿmān b. ʿAmr and not as al-Nuʿaymān, this follows the comment of Ibn Hishām in vol. 1, 703A. A person identified as al-Nuʿmān b. ʿAmr is mention twice in the redaction of Ibn Hishām: on vol. 1, 552A he is identified as a Jew who was one of two Rabbis who questioned Muḥammad and then rejected him. On vol. 1, 703A he is identified as al-Nuʿmān b. ʿAmr b. Rifāʿah b. Sawād, a member of the Sawād b. Mālik b. Ghamm clan, among the Anṣ ār, who participated at Badr. Ibn Hishām, in his commentary, states his name was Nuʿaymān. It is not clear if Ibn Isḥāq understood al-Nuʿmān b. ʿAmr to be the individual who is commonly referred to as being punished for drinking. For passages within the Ibn Isḥāq tradition that identify Nuʿaymān or al-Nuʿaymān with the subject of the person punished for drinking, see via <a href="WSASN.html" class="witness-link">WSASN</a> (Sharīk b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Sharīk al-Najaʿī al-Kūfī): <a href="../references.html#ref-NSKX" class="source-ref">NSKXV05P143B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Nasāʾī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 5 p. 143) and <a href="../references.html#ref-IHMA" class="source-ref">IHMAV12P370B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥāzim</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muḥallā bil-Āthār</span>, vol. 12 p. 370); via the witness of <a href="WZATB.html" class="witness-link">WZATB</a> (Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ṭufayl al-Kūfī al-Bakkāʾī al-ʿĀmirī) (but not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām) <a href="../references.html#ref-NSSX" class="source-ref">NSSXV04P415A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥākim al-Nīsābūrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Mustadrak ʿalā al-ṣaḥīḥīn</span>, vol. 4 p. 415),<a href="../references.html#ref-IHMA" class="source-ref">IHMAV12P370C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥāzim</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muḥallā bil-Āthār</span>, vol. 12 p. 370), <a href="../references.html#ref-BQRX" class="source-ref">BQRXV03P340B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sunan al-ṣaghīr</span>, vol. 3 p. 340), <a href="../references.html#ref-BQSX" class="source-ref">BQSXV08P545B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 8 p. 545), and <a href="../references.html#ref-BQMX" class="source-ref">BQMXV13P039A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Maʿrifat al-sunan waʾl-āthār</span>, vol. 13 p. 39); via the witness of <a href="WYUAU.html" class="witness-link">WYUAU</a> (Yaʿlā b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Umayyah al-Īyādī al-Tanāfisī al-Kūfī), <a href="../references.html#ref-IBAB" class="source-ref">IBABV01P081B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Bishrān</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Amālī Ibn Bishrān</span>, vol. 1 p. 81), <a href="../references.html#ref-BQSX" class="source-ref">BQSXV08P545A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 8 p. 545), and <a href="../references.html#ref-KHTS" class="source-ref">KHTSV04P307A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Ismāʾ al-mubhamah fī al-anbāʾ al-muḥkamah</span>, vol. 4 p. 307); and via <a href="WHSSH.html" class="witness-link">WHSSH</a> (WHSSH): <a href="../references.html#ref-KHTS" class="source-ref">KHTSV04P307B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Ismāʾ al-mubhamah fī al-anbāʾ al-muḥkamah</span>, vol. 4 p. 307) and <a href="../references.html#ref-YNBH" class="source-ref">YNBHV12P358D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-ʿAynī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bināyah sharḥ al-Hidāyah</span>, vol. 12 p. 358). Without a witness, <a href="../references.html#ref-YNBH" class="source-ref">YNBHV12P358A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-ʿAynī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bināyah sharḥ al-Hidāyah</span>, vol. 12 p. 358). For another tradition via <a href="WAYSS.html" class="witness-link">WAYSS</a> (ʿAbd Allāh b. Yazīd b. al-Ṣalt al-Shaybānī) regarding Nuʿaymān&#x27;s role in the fever that struck Madīnah following the migration (the story is found in <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P588A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 588) to vol. 1, 590A without reference to Nuʿaymān), see <a href="../references.html#ref-STJX" class="source-ref">STJXV07P031A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muʿjam al-awsaṭ</span>, vol. 7 p. 31), <a href="../references.html#ref-STBX" class="source-ref">STBXV04P252A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muʿjam al-kabīr</span>, vol. 4 p. 252); without a witness, see <a href="../references.html#ref-HYMZ" class="source-ref">HYMZV02P307A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī b. Abī Bakr Haythamī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Majmaʿ al-zawāʾid wa-manbaʿ al-fawāʾid</span>, vol. 2 p. 307) (quoting al-Ṭabarānī). For a tradition about the story of how Nuʿaymān killed the camel of a Beduoin, via <a href="WJHZA.html" class="witness-link">WJHZA</a> (Jarīr b. Ḥāzim b. Zayd b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Shajāʿ al-Azdī al-ʿAtkī al-Baṣrī), see <a href="../references.html#ref-SBAN" class="source-ref">SBANV01P480A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū al-Shaykh al-Iṣbahānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Akhlāq al-Nabī wa-ādābuhu</span>, vol. 1 p. 480), <a href="../references.html#ref-QZHX" class="source-ref">QZHXV02P302A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Maqrīzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Imtāʿ al-asmāʿ bi-mā li-l-nabī min al-aḥwāl waʾl-amwāl waʾl-hafadat waʾl-mutāʿ</span>, vol. 2 p. 302).

Akhzam al-Ṭāʾī (الهلب بن يزيد بن عدي بن قنافة بن عدي بن عبد شمس بن عدي بن أخزم الطائي). &quot;Al-Hulb&quot; was a nickname, his actual name being Salamah (سلامة). Al-Hulb b. Yazīd al-Ṭāʾī (or Salamah) is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām, nor is his son, Qabīṣah b. Hulb. Note: This passage might go in ritual after pilgrimage section under prayer.

Yaḥyā al-Ghassānī. He died in 135. Yaḥyā b. Yaḥyā is not cited in the redaction of Ibn Hishām.

[^comment-HBHXV43P360A-1]: The passage in <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV43P360A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 43 p. 360) and its variants is placed here due to subject being Abū Rafiʿ and his wife Salamah. The topic of prayer might indicate inclusion in the payer section (above). It is not knowable if it was an original part of one of the original three Ibn Saʿd versions.
[^comment-BKHBV01P249C-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV01P249C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 1 p. 249) is from the biography of Muḥammad b. Nāfiʿ b. ʿUjayr. The passage refers to Suhaymah <em>bint</em> ʿUmayr’s divorce from Rukānah b. ʿAbd Yazīd b. Hāshim. Rukānah is mentioned in <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV02P351A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 2 p. 351) as receiving spoils from Khaybar. Suhaymah is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. The passage is Ibn Isḥāq’s assessment of Nāfiʿ b. ʿUjayr b. ʿAbd Yazīr b. Hāshim. The passage also refers to ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥārith b. ʿUwaymir al-Muzanī. There are several women with the name Suhaymah <em>bint</em> ʿUmayr but with different kunyās, al-Anṣārīyah, al-Muzanīyah, and al-Shaybānīyah. In the story related via Ibn Isḥāq is about Suhaymah al-Muzanīyah, she is married to Rukānah b. ʿAbd Yazīd who announces three declarations of divorce against Suhaymah. The story is related to Ibn Isḥāq by Rukānah’s grandson, ʿAlī b. Yazīd b. Rukānah, or by Suhaymah’s nephew ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥārith b. ʿUwaymir al-Muzanī, Rukānah seeks advice from the prophet about the manner of his divorce. It is clear from this story that it is set in the Madīnan period, although when is not clear. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-LFGH" class="source-ref">LFGHV01P420A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Khalaf b. ʿAbd al-Mālik b. Bashkuwāl</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb Ghawāmiḍ al-asmāʾ al-mubhamah al-wāqiʿah fī mutūn al-aḥādīth al-musnadah</span>, vol. 1 p. 420), the dispute over Suhaymah al-Muzanīyah’s divorce lasted until after the death of Muḥammad and was brought before ʿUmar and ʿUthmān on five different occasions. This is also recounted by <a href="../references.html#ref-THRX" class="source-ref">THRXV07P156A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Athīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Usd al-ghābah fī maʿrifat al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 7 p. 156). Suhaymah <em>bint</em> ʿUmayr al-Anṣārīyah is described as the aunt of ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥārith b. ʿUmayr by <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRS" class="source-ref">HJRSV08P194C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Iṣābah fī tamyīz al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 8 p. 194). Ibn Ḥajar also provides a biographical entry for al-Muzanīyah on the same page, describing her as the wife of Rukānah. He provides different allusions to the divorce issue in both, without mentioning the husband’s name in the entry for al-Anṣārīyah, but saying that al-Muzanīyah took the issue to ʿUmar and ʿUthmān after Muḥammad’s death. This later source seems to separate elements of al-Muzanīyah’s story into one for al-Anṣārīyah, which is related by ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥārith, while the al-Muzanīyah account is related by Nāfiʿ b. ʿUjayr, referenced by Ibn Isḥāq. Suhaymah <em>bint</em> ʿUmayr al-Shaybānīyah had a husband to went of to fight in the military campaigns and did not return. After waiting four years she remained. Shortly after her first husband returned during the Caliphate of ʿUthmān, both husbands traveled to see ʿUthmān to see how the situation should be resolved. He advised them that the first husband had the right to choose either to have his wife or her dowery. This occurred while ʿUthmān was besieged shortly before his death. Afterwards they turned to ʿAlī for advice, who reaffirmed ʿUthmān’s opinion. This story was related by Abū Mulayḥ b. Usāmah (see <a href="../references.html#ref-ADHD" class="source-ref">ADHDV09P695A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn ʿAlī b. Ḥusām al-Dīn ʿAbd al-Mālik Muttaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kanz al-ʿummāl fī sunan al-aqwāl waʾl-afʿāl</span>, vol. 9 p. 695)). A version of this story is provided by <a href="../references.html#ref-THMI" class="source-ref">THMIV02P331B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Ṭaḥāwī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Mukhtaṣar ikhtilāf al-ʿulamāʾ</span>, vol. 2 p. 331) (without a kunyā), also related by Abū Mulayḥ. The evidence suggests that the three people refer to a single individual whose story changed over time. It is not possible to know which version is earliest. Placement in the biography section is due to the present inability to place the text in the narrative.

[^comment-SBDAV01P092A-1]: The <em>isnād</em> after Ibn Isḥāq is حدثنا أحمد بن محمد البغدادي حدثنا عبيد الله بن سعد حدثنا عمي حدثني أبي عن. The passage deals with Muḥammad praying in ʿĀʾishah&#x27;s house. Might also be placed in ritual after <em>hijrah</em>.
[^comment-MNMQV01P215A-1]: ʿĀʾishah is mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām over 60 times.
[^comment-BRSXV04P1913A-1]: The event mentioned at the beginning of the passage in <a href="../references.html#ref-DRQM" class="source-ref">DRQMV02P670A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dāraquṭnī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muʾtalif waʾl-mukhtalif</span>, vol. 2 p. 670) is cited by <a href="../references.html#ref-HHAT" class="source-ref">HHATV02P439A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Razzāq b. Hammām al-Ḥumayrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tafsīr</span>, vol. 2 p. 439), <a href="../references.html#ref-TBJX" class="source-ref">TBJXV17P292A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Jāmiʿ al-bayān ʿan tāʾwīl āy al-Qurʾān</span>, vol. 17 p. 292), <a href="../references.html#ref-RZTX" class="source-ref">RZTXV08P2589A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿaẓīm</span>, vol. 8 p. 2589), and others who cite ʿAbd al-Razzāq b. Hammām al-Ḥumayrī&#x27;s Tafsīr as the source, referring to Qurʾān 24:33. This event or verse is not mention in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. <a href="../references.html#ref-KTMX" class="source-ref">KTMXV01P367A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿUmar b. Shabbah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Kitāb taʾrīkh al-Madīnah al-munawwarah</span>, vol. 1 p. 367) and <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHQ" class="source-ref">KTHQV06P055A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿAẓīm</span>, vol. 6 p. 55) link this event to the Battle of Badr. While this is clearly a biographical entry, Ibn Isḥāq frequently linked events and biographical information together. <a href="../references.html#ref-DRQM" class="source-ref">DRQMV02P670A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Dāraquṭnī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muʾtalif waʾl-mukhtalif</span>, vol. 2 p. 670) will also be placed in the section on the aftermath of Badr. Ibn Isḥāq , in <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV04P300A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 4 p. 300), lists her name as أم الصهباء.
[^comment-BRSXV04P1913C-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-BRSX" class="source-ref">BRSXV04P1913C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Istīʿāb fī maʿrifat al-aṣḥāb</span>, vol. 4 p. 1913) is the biography of Muʿādhah <em>bint</em> ʿAbd Allāh .
